title: 487. Hundred Years' War: Henry V’s Invasion of France (Part 1)

sentences.en: Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more, we'll close the wall up with our English dead.
sentences.zh: 再上前去，亲爱的朋友们，再上前去，我们将用英国阵亡将士的尸体填满城墙。

sentences.en: In peace, there's nothing so becomes a man as modest stillness and humility.
sentences.zh: 在和平时期，没有什么比温和的沉静和谦逊更能衬托出一个人的气质。

sentences.en: But when the blast of war blows in our ears, then imitate the action of the tiger.
sentences.zh: 但当战争的号角在耳畔吹响，就要模仿猛虎的行径。

sentences.en: Stiffen the sinews, summon up the blood, disguise fair nature with hard-favoured rage.
sentences.zh: 绷紧筋骨，振奋精神，用冷酷狰狞的怒容掩饰温和的天性。

sentences.en: I see you stand like greyhounds in the slips, straining upon the start.
sentences.zh: 我看到你们像闸门里蓄势待发的灵缇，迫不及待地想要冲出去。

sentences.en: But the game's afoot.
sentences.zh: 但好戏已经开场了。

sentences.en: Follow your spirit.
sentences.zh: 顺从你们的意志。

sentences.en: And upon this charge, cry God for Harry, England and St. George.
sentences.zh: 趁着这次冲锋，为亨利、英格兰和圣乔治高呼上帝保佑。

sentences.en: Brilliant, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Isn't that basically the whole reason you've done the podcast is so that you can have the chance to read that speech?
sentences.zh: 你做这个播客的全部原因，基本上不就是为了能有机会念这段独白吗？

sentences.en: I've never done that speech before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未念过这段独白。

sentences.en: It's a very moving moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常感人的时刻。

sentences.en: Well, you did it very well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你念得非常好。

sentences.en: Very stirring.
sentences.zh: 非常激昂。

sentences.en: So that is, of course, from Shakespeare's Henry V, the Supreme Epic of English Martial Achievement.
sentences.zh: 所以这段话当然出自莎士比亚的《亨利五世》，英国军事成就的至高史诗。

sentences.en: And that is, Henry, the hero king's call to arms at the siege of Harfleur.
sentences.zh: 而这就是英雄国王亨利在哈夫勒尔围城战中的战斗号召。

sentences.en: And those lines, God for Harry, England and St. George.
sentences.zh: 还有那些台词，为了亨利、英格兰和圣乔治。

sentences.en: That's the kind of thing that you see in tabloid newspaper sports sections when England are about to play the Germans.
sentences.zh: 这正是你在小报体育版上看到的那种内容，当英格兰队即将对阵德国队时。

sentences.en: And our boys have been kicking over tables in peaceful French squares.
sentences.zh: 而我们的同胞一直在宁静的法国广场上掀翻桌子。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, that's one of those Shakespearean lines that, you know, nothing of Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是莎士比亚的名句之一，你知道，即使完全不懂莎士比亚。

sentences.en: You've never seen a single Shakespeare play, but it's entered the folk memory and the national imagination, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 你从未看过哪怕一出莎士比亚戏剧，但它已经进入了民间记忆和民族想象，不是吗？

sentences.en: Even at the most kind of demotic level.
sentences.zh: 即使在最通俗的层面上也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And the setting is the late summer of 1415 and the English under Henry are laying siege to Harfleur, which is a port on the Seine Estuary in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 故事的背景是1415年的夏末，亨利率领的英军正在围攻哈夫勒尔，这是诺曼底塞纳河口的一个港口。

sentences.en: And Henry, by this point, has been king for a couple of years and he's basically a bit bored with just being king of England.
sentences.zh: 而此时的亨利当国王已经有好几年了，他基本上对仅仅做英格兰国王感到有点厌倦。

sentences.en: So he decides that he'd like to be king of France as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定，他也想成为法国国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And launches an invasion.
sentences.zh: 并发动了一场侵略。

sentences.en: But, I mean, he doesn't just decide, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，他可不只是随便决定，汤姆。

sentences.en: He actually is the king of France.
sentences.zh: 他实际上就是法国国王。

sentences.en: He has a perfectly legitimate claim.
sentences.zh: 他有着完全合法的继承权。

sentences.en: He does, of course, which is one that his great-grandfather, Edward III, had been prosecuting as well.
sentences.zh: 他当然有，这也是他的曾祖父爱德华三世一直在主张的权利。

sentences.en: And people who've listened to the four episodes we did on the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 听过我们制作的关于百年战争的四集节目的听众朋友们都知道。

sentences.en: This is basically the Hundred Years' War part two.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是百年战争第二部。

sentences.en: And it's the Hundred Years' War because Henry V decides that he's going to go and attack France because otherwise it would be, you know,
sentences.zh: 之所以被称为百年战争，是因为亨利五世决定去进攻法国，否则它就会变成，你知道的，

sentences.en: 40 Years' War or 60 Years' War or something.
sentences.zh: 40年战争或60年战争之类的。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be nearly as impressive.
sentences.zh: 那样就没那么震撼了。

sentences.en: And I guess that the focus of the previous two episodes for us as English podcasters was the two great victories of Cressy and Poitier.
sentences.zh: 我想，作为英国播客制作者，前两集的焦点是克雷西和普瓦捷这两大战役。

sentences.en: But, of course, the great victory that Henry V wins is probably the most famous of the lot, the Battle of Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 但当然，亨利五世赢得的伟大胜利可能是其中最著名的一场，阿金库尔战役。

sentences.en: Oh, by far.
sentences.zh: 哦，远不止于此。

sentences.en: By far.
sentences.zh: 远远超过。

sentences.en: And in part, it's because it's an even more startling victory.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为这是一场更加惊人的胜利。

sentences.en: But in part, it is also, I think, wouldn't you say, because of Shakespeare, because it's immortalized in this extraordinary play.
sentences.zh: 但部分原因，我认为，你也会这么觉得，是因为莎士比亚，因为它在这部非凡的戏剧中得到了永生。

sentences.en: And his reputation as England's greatest warrior king is completely burnished and gilded by Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 而他作为英格兰最伟大功勋国王的声誉，也被莎士比亚彻底擦亮和镀金了。

sentences.en: It's impossible to say now, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 现在已经无法言说了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's so embedded in the national imagination.
sentences.zh: 因为它已经深深植根于民族想象之中。

sentences.en: Henry V is one of the two or three best-known monarchs of England.
sentences.zh: 亨利五世是英格兰两三个最著名的君主之一。

sentences.en: So, it's impossible to imagine a world in which he wasn't, because we're so used to it.
sentences.zh: 因此，根本无法想象一个没有他的世界，因为我们对此太习以为常了。

sentences.en: So, how much Shakespeare has to do with that?
sentences.zh: 那么，莎士比亚在其中起了多大作用呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I think you're probably right, a lot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想你是对的，作用很大。

sentences.en: And there have been fantastic Shakespearean performances.
sentences.zh: 而且有过非常精彩的莎士比亚戏剧演出。

sentences.en: Kenneth Branagh as Henry V.
sentences.zh: 肯尼思·布拉纳饰演的亨利五世。

sentences.en: Olivier, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然还有劳伦斯·奥利弗。

sentences.en: I mean, Olivier in the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，20世纪40年代的奥利弗。

sentences.en: Dominic, while I was preparing the notes for this, if ever my enthusiasm flagged, I would listen to Kenneth Branagh.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，当我为这期节目准备笔记时，每当我的热情消退，我就会去听肯尼思·布拉纳的录音。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do the We Few, We Happy Few, We Band of Brothers speech on the eve before Agincourt, and it would always revitalize me.
sentences.zh: 在阿金库尔战役的前夜发表那段“我们少数人，我们幸存的少数人，我们生死与共的兄弟”的演讲，这总是能让我重新焕发活力。

sentences.en: So, this is what I think sets the story of Henry V apart from, let's say, the story about Edward III.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我认为将亨利五世的故事与爱德华三世的故事区分开来的地方。

sentences.en: Edward III, an incredibly impressive king, fights the Hundred Years' War, wins lots of battles, all of this.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世，一位极其令人印象深刻的国王，打赢了百年战争，赢得了许多战役，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But Henry V, the idea of the underdog triumph against the odds, the idea of the band of brothers, We Few, We Happy Few.
sentences.zh: 但亨利五世，弱者逆境中取胜的想法，生死兄弟的想法，我们少数人，我们幸存的少数人。

sentences.en: I mean, that obviously plays a part.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这显然起了一定作用。

sentences.en: I mean, Nelson was obsessed with this and the idea of the band of brothers.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊对这一点以及生死兄弟的理念可以说是痴迷。

sentences.en: And then in the Second World War, the idea of The Few, once again, in the Battle of Britain.
sentences.zh: 然后在第二次世界大战中，不列颠之战里又一次出现了“少数人”的概念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That gives it attraction that no other medieval battle has, maybe not even Hastings.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了它任何其他中世纪战役都不具备的吸引力，也许连黑斯廷斯战役都比不上。

sentences.en: Although, Dominic, I mean, of course, the victories won by Edward III and the Black Prince are also very much against the odds
sentences.zh: 尽管，多米尼克，当然，爱德华三世和黑太子所取得的胜利同样也是在逆境中赢得的，

sentences.en: and reflect the fact that England, compared to France, is a relatively minor power.
sentences.zh: 并且反映了这样一个事实：与法国相比，英格兰是一个相对较小的强权。

sentences.en: I mean, it's astonishing that Edward III went to war with France.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世对法国开战，这本身就令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And it's kind of astonishing that Henry V is going to war with France.
sentences.zh: 亨利五世要对法国开战，这也同样令人惊叹。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a big ask.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: But for reasons that we will come to in the course of this episode, it's perhaps not as big an ask as it might have been in the previous century.
sentences.zh: 但出于我们将在本集节目中探讨的原因，这或许不像在上个世纪那样是一个无法完成的任务。

sentences.en: So, let's give it a bit of context.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来交代一下背景。

sentences.en: So, we didn't mention France at all when we were talking about Henry IV.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论亨利四世时，根本没有提到法国。

sentences.en: So, the Usurper King, Battle of Shrewsbury, all that stuff we did last week.
sentences.zh: 也就是篡位者国王、什鲁斯伯里战役，所有我们上周做过的内容。

sentences.en: And partly that's because there has been a kind of a truce in the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为百年战争期间出现了一种休战状态。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a truce, but it's a kind of Cold War as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一场休战，但某种程度上也是一场冷战。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the English are still making a claim, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 因为英格兰人仍在提出领土诉求，对吧？

sentences.en: So, the English kings are still, you know, nominally, they call themselves King of France.
sentences.zh: 所以英国国王们依然，你知道的，名义上自称为法国国王。

sentences.en: And conversely, the French have not accepted the Lancastrians as the rightful kings of England.
sentences.zh: 与此相反，法国人并没有接受兰开斯特家族作为英格兰的正统国王。

sentences.en: They regard Henry IV as Henry of Lancaster rather than King Henry.
sentences.zh: 他们把亨利四世视为兰开斯特的亨利，而不是亨利国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, that's how they always address him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们总是这样称呼他。

sentences.en: And I think that that is partly out of genuine shock that Henry has toppled Richard.
sentences.zh: 我认为这部分是出于对亨利推翻理查德的真正震惊。

sentences.en: The English now have a reputation among the French as people who kill their kings.
sentences.zh: 法国人现在认为英格兰人有弑君的坏名声。

sentences.en: And this is seen as a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: But of course, it's also a way of denying Henry the kind of legitimacy that then he might then capitalize on to start pressing his claim to the throne of France.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这也是一种剥夺亨利合法性的方式，让他无法利用这种合法性来进一步索取法国王位。

sentences.en: And throughout his reign, the French are always in the background.
sentences.zh: 在他的整个统治期间，法国人始终在幕后虎视眈眈。

sentences.en: So, you know, we compared it to the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们把它比作冷战。

sentences.en: The role that they are playing is like the Soviet Union sending military advisors to Vietnam or whatever in the more recent Cold War.
sentences.zh: 他们扮演的角色就像冷战后期苏联向越南派遣军事顾问之类的一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in Scotland, Hotspur's great victory at Humbleton Hill among the captives is a French captain.
sentences.zh: 所以在苏格兰，霍斯珀在汉布尔顿山的伟大胜利中，俘虏中就有一名法国船长。

sentences.en: And in Wales, where Ewing Glyndarr has been leading this incredible rebellion against English rule, the French recognize him as what he claims to be the Prince of Wales in 1404.
sentences.zh: 而在威尔士，欧文·格林杜尔一直在领导这场针对英国统治的惊人叛乱，法国人在1404年承认了他作为威尔士亲王的地位。

sentences.en: And the next year, they actually send a military expedition to Wales.
sentences.zh: 第二年，他们实际上向威尔士派遣了一支远征军。

sentences.en: It lands at Milford Haven and this kind of Franco-Welch force crosses into England, which is almost as far as Worcester.
sentences.zh: 它在米尔福德黑文登陆，这支法威尔联军甚至挺进到了英格兰内部，几乎远至伍斯特。

sentences.en: So, on the British mainland, France is causing trouble.
sentences.zh: 所以在不列颠本土，法国人一直在制造麻烦。

sentences.en: And also in English waters, they're causing trouble.
sentences.zh: 而且在英国海域，他们也在制造麻烦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The English don't have control of the seas, do they?
sentences.zh: 英国人并没有控制海洋，对吧？

sentences.en: The French have control.
sentences.zh: 制海权在法国人手里。

sentences.en: No, they've basically lost it.
sentences.zh: 没有，他们基本上已经失去了制海权。

sentences.en: And Huffler is playing a key role in this.
sentences.zh: 而哈夫勒尔在其中扮演了关键角色。

sentences.en: It's a kind of great nest of pirates, state-sponsored.
sentences.zh: 它是一个巨大的海盗窝，有国家资助的那种。

sentences.en: And it's not just that they're preying on English shipping, but, of course, that they can launch raids on the southern English coaSt.
sentences.zh: 不仅他们一直在掠夺英国船只，而且当然，他们还能对英格兰南部海岸发动袭击。

sentences.en: So, relations aren't great.
sentences.zh: 所以双方关系不太好。

sentences.en: However, the previous two episodes we did on Henry IV, we were talking about how England really has been in a bit of a mess, you know, under Richard II and then under Henry IV.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们在前两集关于亨利四世的节目中谈到过，在理查德二世统治下以及后来的亨利四世统治下，英格兰确实陷入了一团糟。

sentences.en: But it's fair to say, and this, of course, is always a comfort to the English, France, if anything, is in an even bigger mess.
sentences.zh: 但公平地说，这当然总是能给英国人带来一丝安慰，法国如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它陷入了更严重的混乱。

sentences.en: The French king, unlike Henry, Henry IV, and, of course, Henry V as his son, he doesn't have a crisis of legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 法国国王与亨利、亨利四世以及作为他儿子的亨利五世不同，他没有合法性危机。

sentences.en: But I think it would be fair to say he's not 100% on top of his game.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，他的状态并非百分之百在线。

sentences.en: And, in fact, maybe of all the French kings, he is the man who could best do with a subscription to BetterHelp.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在所有的法国国王中，他可能是最需要购买心理咨询服务的那个。

sentences.en: BetterHelp?
sentences.zh: 心理咨询服务？

sentences.en: I was thinking exactly that.
sentences.zh: 我刚才也正是这么想的。

sentences.en: Yeah, his mental health is very, very frail.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的精神状况非常非常脆弱。

sentences.en: He is in a terrible mess, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他真是糟糕透顶了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, Charles VI, he'd become king in 1380, and he was king for, you know, six centuries or something.
sentences.zh: 所以，查理六世在1380年成为国王，他当了，你知道的，六个世纪左右的国王。

sentences.en: Yeah, when he was 12.
sentences.zh: 是的，他登基时才12岁。

sentences.en: And, you know, we talked in the French Revolution, didn't we, about how French kings tend to be young.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们在讲法国大革命时讨论过，法国国王往往都很年轻，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But he's always having these breakdowns, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他总是精神崩溃，对吧？

sentences.en: And the first one I read, 1392, it's because he's approached by a leper in a wood, and that causes him to have a nervous breakdown.
sentences.zh: 我读到的第一次是在1392年，原因是在树林里遇到一个麻风病人，这导致他神经崩溃。

sentences.en: Extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: He's on a military expedition, I think going off to Brittany, and it's very, very hot.
sentences.zh: 他当时正进行一次军事远征，我想是去布列塔尼，天气非常非常热。

sentences.en: He's getting, you know, increasingly stressed, and this leper looms out, grabs the bridle of his horse, and cries out, you are betrayed.
sentences.zh: 他变得，你知道的，越来越紧张，然后这个麻风病人突然出现，抓住他马的缰绳大喊，你被背叛了。

sentences.en: And the king has this nervous breakdown, and he takes to bed for several weeks.
sentences.zh: 然后国王精神崩溃了，卧床好几个星期。

sentences.en: And then it seems that he's recovered from this.
sentences.zh: 后来他似乎从这次发作中恢复了过来。

sentences.en: And then the next year, something even worse happens, which we actually discussed in our episode on the worst parties in history.
sentences.zh: 但在第二年，发生了更糟糕的事情，我们实际上在关于历史最差派对的那期节目中讨论过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's called by the French, the Balle des Ardents, the Ball of the Burning Men.
sentences.zh: 法国人称之为“炽人舞会”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And people may remember that it's a big party.
sentences.zh: 大家可能还记得，那是一个盛大的派对。

sentences.en: The king and five of his lords decide that they will dress up as wild men of the woods, and they coat themselves in tar, and then stick branches and leaves onto themselves.
sentences.zh: 国王和他的五位领主决定扮成森林里的野人，他们在身上涂满柏油，然后把树枝和树叶粘在身上。

sentences.en: And obviously, they're aware that this is a little bit dangerous.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们知道这有点危险。

sentences.en: So the king says, whatever you do, you know, turn out all the candles, you can't have the candles.
sentences.zh: 所以国王说，无论你们做什么，你知道的，把所有的蜡烛都熄灭，绝对不能有蜡烛。

sentences.en: And then his younger brother, Louis, the Duke of Orléans, comes in, says, oh, what are those costumes?
sentences.zh: 然后他的弟弟，奥尔良公爵路易走了进来，说，哦，这些是什么服装？

sentences.en: He's got a torch, puts the torch up to look at them.
sentences.zh: 他拿着一支火炬，把火炬凑近去打量他们。

sentences.en: And he just goes, whoosh.
sentences.zh: 结果轰的一下。

sentences.en: And, you know, four of them burn to death, and only the king and one other lord whose robes have caught fire survive.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，其中四人被活活烧死，只有国王和另一位长袍着火的领主幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Hot, hot, hot.
sentences.zh: 太热了，太热了，太热了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's not helpful to his mental stability at all.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他心理的稳定性毫无帮助。

sentences.en: And by 1395, so two years on, he's claiming that he's St. George.
sentences.zh: 到了1395年，也就是两年后，他声称自己是圣乔治。

sentences.en: He then starts worrying that he's made of glass.
sentences.zh: 接着他开始担心自己是玻璃做的。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: He worries that he's made of glass.
sentences.zh: 他担心自己是玻璃做的。

sentences.en: So we talked about that, I think, also with Bart van Leeu, when we talked about Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们在谈论勃艮第时，和巴特·范·莱乌也讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very anxious, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常焦虑，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he basically wants to be literally wrapped in cotton wool.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他基本上希望自己字面意义上被包裹在医用棉花里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because if you're made of glass, anything could shatter you.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是由玻璃做成的，任何东西都能把你粉碎。

sentences.en: And obviously, I mean, this isn't an ideal condition if you're the king of medieval France, being menaced by England and a host of other enemies.
sentences.zh: 很显然，我的意思是，如果你是中世纪的法国国王，面临着来自英格兰和许多其他敌人的威胁，这可不是什么理想的状况。

sentences.en: But nobody thinks to depose him.
sentences.zh: 但没有人想要废黜他。

sentences.en: So he is called Charles the Mad, but he's also called Charles the Beloved.
sentences.zh: 所以他被称为疯子查理，但他也被称为受爱戴的查理。

sentences.en: And actually, when he's lucid, he's perfectly competent.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当他清醒的时候，他完全称职。

sentences.en: But the problem is, as the years go by, the periods of lucidity become fewer and fewer and shorter and shorter.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，随着时间的推移，清醒的时期变得越来越少，也越来越短。

sentences.en: And so the fact that the king is basically, you know, out of action makes faction fighting kind of inevitable, because that's always what happens.
sentences.zh: 因此，国王基本上，你知道的，无法履行职责，这就使得派系斗争在某种程度上变得不可避免，因为事情总是这样发展。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there are two great factions, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 所以有两大派系，对吧？

sentences.en: Each of them is led by a charismatic and very formidable character.
sentences.zh: 他们每一个人都由一个充满个人魅力且非常可怕的人物领导。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Both of whom are members of the royal family.
sentences.zh: 这两人都是王室成员。

sentences.en: So let's start with the first one.
sentences.zh: 那我们先从第一个开始。

sentences.en: The first one is Louis, the Duke of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 第一个是奥尔良公爵路易。

sentences.en: Now, he has slightly got a he's got a bit of a tarnished reputation because he's the fellow with the torch at the Ball des Ardents, the ball of the burning men.
sentences.zh: 现在，他的名声有点受损，因为他就是野人舞会上那个拿着火炬的家伙，也就是燃烧之人的舞会。

sentences.en: So he's a cad, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他是个浪荡子，对吧？

sentences.en: Or is he a bounder?
sentences.zh: 还是说他是个无赖？

sentences.en: Hard to tell the difference.
sentences.zh: 很难看出区别。

sentences.en: I think he's more of a cad.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他更像个浪荡子。

sentences.en: So he's a massive womanizer.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个十足的好色之徒。

sentences.en: So Thomas Wilsingham, the monk at St. Albans, who we've been drawing on a lot for these episodes, describes him as a man who is always taking his pleasure with whores,
sentences.zh: 因此，圣奥尔本斯的修道士托马斯·威尔辛厄姆——我们在这些节目中经常引用他的记载——将他描述为一个总是与妓女、娼妇和乱伦行乐的人。

sentences.en: harlots and inceSt.
sentences.zh: 乱伦。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And the charge of incest relates to the fact that he's said to have had an affair with the queen.
sentences.zh: 而乱伦的指控则源于这样一个事实，即据说他与王后有染。

sentences.en: So his sister.
sentences.zh: 也就是他的嫂子。

sentences.en: But he's French.
sentences.zh: 但他是法国人。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this comes with the territory, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这很正常，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, one may think that.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们可能会这么想。

sentences.en: And he'd been a very good friend of Henry of Lancaster before Henry became king and while he was in exile.
sentences.zh: 在亨利成为国王之前以及他流亡期间，路易曾是兰开斯特的亨利非常好的朋友。

sentences.en: And then, of course, Henry goes off and deposes Richard II.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，亨利离开并废黜了理查二世。

sentences.en: And Orléans feels incredibly insulted by this.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良对此感到极其愤怒。

sentences.en: He feels that Henry has stabbed him in the back, that he's betrayed him.
sentences.zh: 他觉得亨利在背后捅了他一刀，觉得亨利背叛了他。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: It's not all about him.
sentences.zh: 这又不全关他的事。

sentences.en: As far as he's concerned, it is about him because he's getting criticised in France for the role that he's supposed to have played in the deposition of Richard II.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，这确实关他的事，因为他在法国受到了批评，原因是他被认为在废黜理查二世的事件中扮演了角色。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, the kind of the vigour of his hostility to Henry IV is an attempt to try and demonstrate the fact that he wasn't complicit in Henry's coup.
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，他对亨利四世表现出的强烈敌意，其实是想试图证明他并未参与亨利的政变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Thomas, a little bit like if you launched a coup and I was embarrassed that you'd done this, I might then try to distance myself from you.
sentences.zh: 所以，托马斯，这有点像如果你发动了一场政变，而我为你做了这件事感到尴尬，我可能就会试图与你保持距离。

sentences.en: But then, kind of massively overcompensated and challenged you to a duel.
sentences.zh: 但随后又反应过度，向你发起了决斗挑战。

sentences.en: Because this is what Louis of Orléans does, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为这就是奥尔良的路易会做的事，对吧？

sentences.en: Literally, yeah.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，是的。

sentences.en: He writes to Henry and says, let's settle this, man to man.
sentences.zh: 他写信给亨利说，让我们堂堂正正地解决这件事。

sentences.en: You've let me down here.
sentences.zh: 你这次真让我失望。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Henry says, no, not having any of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，而亨利说，门都没有。

sentences.en: But I think that exchange reflects Louis' character.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这段对话反映了路易的性格。

sentences.en: He's very hot-headed.
sentences.zh: 他非常冲动。

sentences.en: He's very patriotic.
sentences.zh: 他非常爱国。

sentences.en: He's a man who enjoys holding a grudge and nursing it.
sentences.zh: 他是个喜欢记仇并把仇恨深埋心底的人。

sentences.en: I like him.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢他的。

sentences.en: But he's also kind of very subtle and sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 但他也相当机敏和老练。

sentences.en: So, a slight Captain Benteen quality to him, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 所以，他身上或许带有一点本廷上尉的特质。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Sounds great.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒。

sentences.en: With the additional bonus of setting fire to people dressed in pitch.
sentences.zh: 附带的福利是给那些穿着沥青衣服的人放火。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And also the harlots and the incest, which Captain Benteen was a stranger to.
sentences.zh: 还有那些妓女和乱伦，本廷上尉对此可是全然不知。

sentences.en: Yes, let's put that on the record.
sentences.zh: 是的，让我们把这记入史册。

sentences.en: So, very much not the kind of person who would tolerate a rival.
sentences.zh: 因此，他绝对不是那种会容忍竞争对手的人。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, he does have a rival in the French court.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，他在法国宫廷里确实有一个对手。

sentences.en: And this is in the form of John the Fearless.
sentences.zh: 那就是无畏者约翰。

sentences.en: And you mentioned Bart van Leeu, who did one of our iconic early episodes, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 你提到了巴特·范·莱尤，他制作了我们早期的标志性节目之一，对吧？

sentences.en: On the Dukes of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 关于勃艮第公爵的节目。

sentences.en: And John the Fearless is the son of the first great Duke of Burgundy, who was Philip the Bold, who was the youngest son of Charles V.
sentences.zh: 而无畏者约翰是第一位伟大的勃艮第公爵大胆的菲利普的儿子，大胆的菲利普是查理五世的小儿子。

sentences.en: So, Philip the Bold was the uncle of Charles VI.
sentences.zh: 所以，大胆的菲利普是查理六世的叔叔。

sentences.en: So, John the Fearless is Charles VI's cousin.
sentences.zh: 因此，无畏者约翰是查理六世的表弟。

sentences.en: And John the Fearless rules this enormous agglomeration of territories.
sentences.zh: 无畏者约翰统治着这片庞大得惊人的领土。

sentences.en: Of all the French peers, he's the guy who has the largest land and property.
sentences.zh: 在所有的法国贵族中，他是拥有最多土地和财产的人。

sentences.en: So, it includes not just Burgundy, but also the county of Flanders.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅包括勃艮第，还包括佛兰德斯伯国。

sentences.en: And over the course of his father's life and his own life, John the Fearless kind of basically, I mean, he comes to rule pretty much the whole of the Low Countries.
sentences.zh: 在他父亲的有生之年以及他自己的有生之年，无畏者约翰基本上——我的意思是，他最终统治了几乎整个低地国家。

sentences.en: And of course, that then embroils him in English politics, because the Low Countries are crucial to the wool trade.
sentences.zh: 当然，这随后使他卷入了英国政治，因为低地国家对羊毛贸易至关重要。

sentences.en: So, the Dukes of Burgundy are always kind of midway a bit between France and England.
sentences.zh: 因此，勃艮第公爵总是处于法国和英国之间。

sentences.en: And this is an important part of the story.
sentences.zh: 这是故事的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: So, to survey the scene, we've got Charles VI, who thinks he's made a glass and is bonkers.
sentences.zh: 所以，纵观全局，我们有查理六世，他觉得自己是玻璃做的，而且疯了。

sentences.en: And then we've got the two power brokers who are fighting for control in France.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有两名在法国争夺控制权的权力掮客。

sentences.en: Louis of Orléans, incest, burning torches and grudges.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的路易：乱伦、燃烧的火炬和记恨。

sentences.en: John the Fearless, literally fearless, rules Burgundy and the Low Countries.
sentences.zh: 无畏者约翰：名副其实的无畏，统治着勃艮第和低地国家。

sentences.en: And for those two guys, the important thing is who's going to control the heir to the throne.
sentences.zh: 对这两个家伙来说，最重要的事情是谁将控制王位继承人。

sentences.en: The Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 王太子。

sentences.en: Because do they assume that the Mad King is not long for this world?
sentences.zh: 因为他们是否认为疯王时日无多？

sentences.en: I think it's the fact that with the king out of action, and the Dauphin is quite young.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是因为国王无法理政，而王太子还很年轻。

sentences.en: He's not even a teenager at this point.
sentences.zh: 他此时甚至还没到少年时期。

sentences.en: If you can get him under his thumb, then basically you have the rule of France.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把他控制在手掌心，基本上你就统治了法国。

sentences.en: And the Dauphin is not a hugely impressive figure.
sentences.zh: 而且王太子并不是一个给人留下深刻印象的人物。

sentences.en: So, he will grow up to become an absolutely classic teenager.
sentences.zh: 所以，他长大后会变成一个绝对典型的青少年。

sentences.en: Very kind of sulky, moody, getting up at midday.
sentences.zh: 非常阴郁、喜怒无常、中午才起床。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A bit fat, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，有点胖。

sentences.en: People are always commenting on this.
sentences.zh: 人们总是在议论这个。

sentences.en: Tom, you're fat shamed of the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你在对外貌羞辱王太子。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it's not me.
sentences.zh: 好吧，又不是我说的。

sentences.en: I'm merely quoting his contemporaries.
sentences.zh: 我只是在引用他同时代人的话。

sentences.en: And so, certainly at this age, he's quite a cipher as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，至少在这个年龄，他也完全是个无足轻重的人。

sentences.en: And so, as a result, the Orleanists and the Burgundians are just kind of endlessly kidnapping the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 因此，奥尔良派和勃艮第派就不断地绑架王太子。

sentences.en: And it's all quite bewildering.
sentences.zh: 这一切都相当令人眼花缭乱。

sentences.en: They really need to kind of keep track of all the ins and outs of it.
sentences.zh: 他们确实需要弄清楚其中的所有来龙去脉。

sentences.en: But it's John the Fearless who essentially emerges triumphant from this tit-for-the-tat Dauphin kidnapping.
sentences.zh: 但最终从这场你来我往的王太子绑架战中胜出的人是无畏者约翰。

sentences.en: Because he gets himself appointed guardian of the Dauphin while the king is off being mad.
sentences.zh: 因为趁着国王发疯的时候，他让自己被任命为了王太子的监护人。

sentences.en: And Orlean, the Duke of Orlean, responds to this in 1407 in a very decisive way.
sentences.zh: 而奥尔良公爵在1407年对此做出了果断的回应。

sentences.en: He has a clean out of the Royal Council.
sentences.zh: 他对皇家委员会进行了一次大清洗。

sentences.en: And almost all the Burgundian sympathizers are kicked off.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的勃艮第同情者都被驱逐了。

sentences.en: And then he uses the Royal Treasury to buy himself the Duchy of Luxembourg, which basically straddles the two territories that the Duke of Burgundy rules.
sentences.zh: 然后他动用国库为自己买下了卢森堡公国，该公国基本上地跨勃艮第公爵统治的两块领地。

sentences.en: So, in the Low Countries and in Burgundy proper.
sentences.zh: 也就是低地国家和勃艮第本土。

sentences.en: And this is infuriating to John the Fearless.
sentences.zh: 这把无畏者约翰气坏了。

sentences.en: And they're gearing up, you know, to have another crack at each other.
sentences.zh: 他们正在摩拳擦掌，准备再大干一场。

sentences.en: And Charles VI comes out of his madness.
sentences.zh: 而查理六世的病情好转了。

sentences.en: And on the 20th of November, 1407, he summons the two Dukes into his presence.
sentences.zh: 1407年11月20日，他召集两位公爵来到自己面前。

sentences.en: And he presides over a very solemn reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 他主持了一场非常庄严的和解仪式。

sentences.en: And it ends with him saying, now, praise be God.
sentences.zh: 仪式以他的一句话结束：现在，赞美上帝。

sentences.en: You know, you have sworn solemn oaths.
sentences.zh: 你们已经发了庄严的誓言。

sentences.en: All is good.
sentences.zh: 一切都很好。

sentences.en: And then three days later, Orlean is murdered in Paris by 15 masked assassins as he is mounting his horse.
sentences.zh: 然而三天后，奥尔良在巴黎骑马时遭到15名蒙面刺客的谋杀。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 真是个反转。

sentences.en: And the assassins get arrested.
sentences.zh: 刺客被捕了。

sentences.en: And it turns out that the guy in charge of these assassins is a personal servant of John the Fearless.
sentences.zh: 结果发现领导这些刺客的人是无畏者约翰的私人仆人。

sentences.en: So, it's pretty clear who's behind it.
sentences.zh: 所以，幕后黑手是谁显而易见。

sentences.en: And in fact, John the Fearless doesn't deny it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，无畏者约翰也并未否认。

sentences.en: He commissions a professor at the Sorbonne to deliver a public lecture on tyrannicide and how it's justified.
sentences.zh: 他委任索福隆的一位教授发表了一场关于弑君以及如何将其合理化的公开演讲。

sentences.en: And you would think that for the king to have to swallow this as he does is an abject humiliation.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，国王不得不咽下这口气——正如他所做的那样——是一种极大的羞辱。

sentences.en: And it is.
sentences.zh: 事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: But the reason he does it is that he knows that if he doesn't, then there will be civil war.
sentences.zh: 但他这么做的原因在于，他知道如果他不这么做，就会爆发内战。

sentences.en: And so, the king issues John the Fearless with an official pardon in the spring of 1408.
sentences.zh: 于是，国王在1408年春向无畏者约翰颁发了官方特赦令。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Orlean, he was the king's, what relative was he to the king?
sentences.zh: 奥尔良，他是国王的什么人，他是国王的什么亲戚？

sentences.en: His brother.
sentences.zh: 他的弟弟。

sentences.en: His younger brother.
sentences.zh: 他的亲弟弟。

sentences.en: He was his brother.
sentences.zh: 他是他的弟弟。

sentences.en: So, his brother has been murdered by 15 masked men.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的弟弟被15个蒙面人谋杀了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he gives the bloke who did it a pardon just because he's frightened of him.
sentences.zh: 而他竟然仅仅因为害怕凶手，就特赦了那个干这事的家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, that's weak.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这太懦弱了。

sentences.en: Well, because not so much that he's worried about John the Fearless, but that he doesn't want France to collapse into civil war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，与其说他是担心无畏者约翰，不如说他是不想让法国陷入内战。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And John the Fearless, who's incredibly unscrupulous and very, very good at kind of pushing what he can do just far enough, he realizes this.
sentences.zh: 而无畏者约翰极其寡廉鲜耻，并且非常擅长将自己的所作所为推到刚刚好的极限，他意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And so, by November 1408, he's installed himself in Paris as the big man.
sentences.zh: 因此，到1408年11月，他已经在巴黎稳居大权在握的地位。

sentences.en: And 1409, he forces the king to issue him another formal pardon in Chartres Cathedral.
sentences.zh: 1409年，他迫使国王在沙特尔大教堂向他颁发了另一份正式特赦令。

sentences.en: And also there in Chartres on that day is the new Duke of Orleans, who's called Charles, who at this point is only 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 那天在沙特尔的还有新任奥尔良公爵，名叫查理，他此时年仅15岁。

sentences.en: And when John the Fearless is given this pardon, it's said that he approaches the young son of the murdered Duke of Orleans, Charles, the new Duke of Orleans.
sentences.zh: 据说当无畏者约翰获得这纸特赦时，他走向了被谋杀的奥尔良公爵的年轻儿子、新任奥尔良公爵查理。

sentences.en: He's only 15 years at this time.
sentences.zh: 他当时只有15岁。

sentences.en: So, he's had a very, very kind of brutal baptism into being the Duke of Orleans.
sentences.zh: 所以，他作为奥尔良公爵的开端经历了一场非常非常残酷的洗礼。

sentences.en: And he approaches him and he's got tears streaming down his face.
sentences.zh: 他向查理走去，脸上挂满泪水。

sentences.en: And he says, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 他说，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Please forgive me.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我。

sentences.en: So, sorry I killed your father.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉杀了你父亲。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, but let's kiss and make up, you know, water under the bridge.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，但让我们重修旧好吧，过去的事就让它过去吧。

sentences.en: Let's move on.
sentences.zh: 让我们向前看。

sentences.en: And he asks for Orleans forgiveness and Orleans refuses, even though he's only 15.
sentences.zh: 他请求奥尔良的原谅，但奥尔良拒绝了，尽管他才15岁。

sentences.en: And the king says, no, you've got to kiss and make up.
sentences.zh: 国王说，不，你们得握手言和。

sentences.en: So, they do.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们照做了。

sentences.en: But I think it's pretty clear that Orleans is biding his time, even though it seems that John is now completely triumphant because he's got the king under his thumb.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很明显，奥尔良在等待时机，尽管约翰现在似乎完全大获全胜，因为他把国王玩弄于股掌之间。

sentences.en: He's the sole guardian of the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 他是王太的唯一监护人。

sentences.en: He occupies Paris.
sentences.zh: 他占领了巴黎。

sentences.en: It all seems brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这一切看起来都很辉煌。

sentences.en: But the new Duke of Orleans is not taking it, lying down.
sentences.zh: 但新任奥尔良公爵并没有逆来顺受。

sentences.en: So, in 1410, he leaves Paris and he goes to Guillaume, which is about 50 miles east of Orleans.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1410年，他离开巴黎，前往吉约姆，那大约在奥尔良以东50英里处。

sentences.en: He's 16 by now.
sentences.zh: 他此时16岁。

sentences.en: And he marries a girl called Bon.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一个名叫博恩的女孩。

sentences.en: She's only 11.
sentences.zh: 她才11岁。

sentences.en: But, you know, that's kind of standard behavior for this time.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这在当时算是一种标准操作。

sentences.en: Bon is the daughter of the Count of Armagnac, who is the constable of France and very subtle, very skillful, kind of little finger from Game of Thrones type character.
sentences.zh: 博恩是阿马尼亚克伯爵的女儿，阿马尼亚克伯爵是法国王室统帅，非常狡猾、非常老练，有点像《权力的游戏》里那种能翻云覆雨的角色。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: A shrewd operator.
sentences.zh: 一个精明的操盘手。

sentences.en: And so, Armagnac has invited, as well as the young Duke of Orleans, he's invited various other dukes,
sentences.zh: 所以，阿马尼亚克不仅邀请了年轻的奥尔良公爵，还邀请了其他多位公爵，

sentences.en: various other counts to attend the wedding because it's an ideal opportunity for them all to sign up to a kind of anti-Burgundian alliance.
sentences.zh: 多位伯爵来参加婚礼，因为这对他们所有人来说都是一个绝佳的机会，可以加入某种反勃艮第同盟。

sentences.en: And there is one other figure, as well as Orleans, the young Duke of Orleans and Armagnac.
sentences.zh: 除了奥尔良、年轻的奥尔良公爵和阿马尼亚克之外，还有另一个重要人物。

sentences.en: And this is the Count of Alençon, who is a great landholder in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿朗松伯爵，诺曼底的一位大领主。

sentences.en: And he is, I mean, he's an absolute bruiser.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他绝对是个狠角色。

sentences.en: He's very bold.
sentences.zh: 他非常大胆。

sentences.en: He's very aggressive.
sentences.zh: 他非常具有攻击性。

sentences.en: He's kind of compared to a raging bore.
sentences.zh: 他有点像一头暴怒的公牛。

sentences.en: And it's said of him by a contemporary chronicler that without Alençon, the good and holy cause of Orleans could not have been sustained.
sentences.zh: 一位当代编年史家这样评价他：如果没有阿朗松，奥尔良美好而神圣的事业就无法维持下去。

sentences.en: So with this body of very heavyweight allies now behind him, Orleans starts preparing for revenge.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些重量级盟友的支持下，奥尔良开始筹备复仇。

sentences.en: And Burgundy is warned about this.
sentences.zh: 勃艮第收到了风声。

sentences.en: So he starts recruiting troops.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始招募军队。

sentences.en: And it's said that there are so many soldiers out and about that people in France assume that there's an English invasion coming.
sentences.zh: 据说当时四处都是士兵，以至于法国人以为英国军队要入侵了。

sentences.en: So the two sides, Orleans, the young teenager who's lost his father and his wife and their hangers-on and all these cronies that went to the wedding and the Alençon.
sentences.zh: 所以这两派人马是：奥尔良，那个失去了父亲和妻子的年轻少年，还有他们的随从、所有去参加婚礼的亲信，以及阿朗松。

sentences.en: And they're the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 他们就是阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: Yes, because of the Count of Armagnac.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为阿马尼亚克伯爵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the other side, you have the Burgundians.
sentences.zh: 而在另一边，则是勃艮第派。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But crucially, the Burgundians have under their power the king and the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 但关键是，勃艮第派控制着国王和王太子。

sentences.en: So they can paint the Armagnacs as insurgents, as rebels, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上可以把阿马尼亚克派描绘成暴徒、叛军。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this is obviously brilliant for England.
sentences.zh: 对英国来说，这显然是个绝佳的机会。

sentences.en: And for Henry IV, who's been having a rough time of it.
sentences.zh: 对于一直过得不太顺的亨利四世来说也是如此。

sentences.en: But it means that he can kind of fish in troubled waters because both sides are appealing to him for assistance.
sentences.zh: 但这意味他可以在浑水里摸鱼，因为双方都在向他寻求援助。

sentences.en: So what Henry does, he sends two expeditions to France.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利的做法是，向法国派遣了两次远征军。

sentences.en: He sends one in 1411 on the side of Burgundy and against the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 他在1411年派了一支，站在勃艮第这一边，对抗阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: And then he sends one in 1412 against the Burgundians and on the side of the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 然后在1412年又派了一支，对抗勃艮第派，站在阿马尼亚克派这一边。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 绝妙。

sentences.en: That's excellent diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 这是极高明的外交手腕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And basically, he's doing that because both sides are, you know, they're offering him enormous bribes.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他这么做是因为双方都在给他提供巨大的贿赂，你知道的。

sentences.en: They're offering him all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们向他许诺各种好处。

sentences.en: And so he pays them off against each other.
sentences.zh: 因此他利用双方互相制衡。

sentences.en: And actually, he ends up basically being promised the whole of the Duchy of Aquitaine,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最终几乎得到了整个阿基坦公国的承诺，

sentences.en: which was the lands that were the kind of ancestral fiefdom of the kings of England and which Edward III had aggrandized.
sentences.zh: 那里的土地是英格兰国王的祖传封地，曾被爱德华三世大大扩张过。

sentences.en: He'd been given an enormous tranche and the French had then whittled away.
sentences.zh: 他曾获得过大片领地，后来被法国人蚕食了。

sentences.en: So, you know, this is looking great for Henry IV.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这对亨利四世来说是个好兆头。

sentences.en: And you'd think also that it would be the perfect opportunity for Henry to blood his eldest son, the Prince of Wales, the future Henry V.
sentences.zh: 你也会觉得，这也是亨利让他的长子——威尔士亲王、未来的亨利五世——历练一番的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: But interestingly, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他没有这么做。

sentences.en: And this may well reflect the fact that, as we talked about in the previous episode, relations between father and elder son by this point seem to have become quite troubled.
sentences.zh: 这很可能反映了一个事实，正如我们在上一集里讨论过的，到这个时候，父子关系似乎已经变得相当紧张了。

sentences.en: But what Henry does, he sends two people, both of whom are very close friends of Henry.
sentences.zh: 但亨利的做法是，派了两个人去，这两人都是亨利的至交好友。

sentences.en: Both of them are called Thomas, I'm pleased to say.
sentences.zh: 很高兴地说，他们都叫托马斯。

sentences.en: So the first of them, the one who goes in 1411, is the Earl of Arundel, who had served with the Prince of Wales in Wales, one of his closest friends.
sentences.zh: 他们中的第一个，也就是1411年去的那位，是阿伦德尔伯爵，他曾在威尔士跟随威尔士亲王作战，是亲王最亲密的朋友之一。

sentences.en: And the second is the eldest of his three younger brothers, Thomas, the Duke of Clarence.
sentences.zh: 第二位是他三个弟弟中的长子，托马斯，克拉伦斯公爵。

sentences.en: And for Clarence, it's very, very annoying because he arrives in France at the head of this great expedition only to find that the two sides have made up again.
sentences.zh: 对克拉伦斯来说，这非常非常恼火，因为他率领着这支庞大的远征军抵达法国，却发现双方又和好了。

sentences.en: So they've signed a compact.
sentences.zh: 所以他们签署了一项协议。

sentences.en: And Ollion is incredibly apologetic, says, you know, I'm really sorry you won't have a chance to go out and sort of loot and stuff.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良感到非常抱歉，说，你知道的，真的很抱歉，你们没有机会出去掠夺一番了。

sentences.en: But he gives Clarence a massive payoff.
sentences.zh: 但他给了克拉伦斯一大笔丰厚的报酬。

sentences.en: The two men become sworn brothers in arms and Clarence swears a formal oath that he will serve aid, console and comfort.
sentences.zh: 两人结为誓同生死的手足兄弟，克拉伦斯正式发誓他将提供援助、安慰和抚慰。

sentences.en: And he then goes back to England and he's loaded down with booty, even though he hasn't fought a single battle, he hasn't captured a single town.
sentences.zh: 然后他带着满载的战利品回到英格兰，尽管他没有打过一场仗，也没有攻占过一座城镇。

sentences.en: And it's a reminder to the English court of just how many riches are on offer in France.
sentences.zh: 这提醒了英国宫廷，法国到底有多少财富可图。

sentences.en: And so when Henry V comes to the throne, he's all the more alert than he would have been anyway to the opportunities on offer.
sentences.zh: 因此，当亨利五世登基时，他对法国的机会比以前更加敏锐。

sentences.en: And, you know, he can see in the loot that Clarence has brought back that the civil war in France absolutely promises an opportunity to win not just booty,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，从克拉伦斯带回的战利品中，他可以看出法国的内战绝对带来了不仅能赢得战利品，

sentences.en: but possibly land as well.
sentences.zh: 而且可能赢得土地的机会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So it's that classic thing of a great sort of continental power that is riven by internal tension and a kind of offshore smaller power that sees the opportunity to basically carve out.
sentences.zh: 所以这就呈现出那种经典模式：一个内部矛盾重重的庞大欧洲大陆强国，和一个看到了可以借此分一杯羹的机会的海外小国。

sentences.en: So it's a little bit kind of Japan and China in the 20th century or something.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像20世纪的日本和中国之类的情况。

sentences.en: Well, the problem for France is that Henry's crowned on the 9th of April, 1413.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对法国来说，问题在于亨利在1413年4月9日加冕。

sentences.en: There's a kind of unseasonal snowstorm and contemporaries are unclear whether this is a good or bad omen.
sentences.zh: 当时下了一场反季节的暴风雪，同时代的人不清楚这是好兆头还是坏兆头。

sentences.en: But what is very clear is that the new king is very, very formidable.
sentences.zh: 但非常清楚的是，这位新国王极其强悍。

sentences.en: So he's 26 by this point.
sentences.zh: 此时他26岁。

sentences.en: He's battle-hardened.
sentences.zh: 他久经沙场。

sentences.en: He's skilled in all the practicalities of kingship because he's effectively been ruling for long stretches of his father's reign.
sentences.zh: 他精通治国理政的各种实际操作，因为在他父亲统治的大部分时间里，他实际上一直在执政。

sentences.en: He's a man of absolutely iron determination, extraordinary capabilities.
sentences.zh: 他是一个意志坚如钢铁、能力非凡的人。

sentences.en: So in every way, if there is a man who is qualified to exploit the divisions in France, it is the new king of England.
sentences.zh: 因此，从各方面来看，如果说有谁具备利用法国分裂局势的资格，那就是这位英格兰新国王。

sentences.en: Well, that's good to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这个消息真好。

sentences.en: That's very promising.
sentences.zh: 这很有希望。

sentences.en: And it bodes well for the second half of this episode, in which we will discover if Henry V is indeed the man to profit from the internal divisions of France.
sentences.zh: 这也预示着本集下半部分将会非常精彩，我们将探讨亨利五世是否真的是那个能从法国内部裂痕中获利的人。

sentences.en: Come back after the break and find out.
sentences.zh: 休息片刻，马上回来揭晓。

sentences.zh: 英国与俄罗斯之间的战略较量。

sentences.zh: 首相先生，我们高度确信这是俄罗斯干的。

sentences.zh: 让俄罗斯人承担责任就等于引发第三次世界大战。

sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那个人在玩火，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，你想玩吗？

sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！

sentences.zh: 我们需要理解政策背景。

sentences.zh: 今天，所有相关背景都将被构建为一个框架。

sentences.zh: 并传达到作战命令中。

sentences.zh: 也就是作战补充指令。

sentences.zh: 感谢他的礼物和你们的辛劳。

sentences.zh: 当我们把球拍对准这些网球，凭着上帝的恩典，我们将在法国打上一场球赛，把他的王冠击落入险境。

sentences.en: So that's one of the most famous episodes in Shakespeare's play, Henry V.
sentences.zh: 所以这是莎士比亚戏剧《亨利五世》中最著名的情节之一。

sentences.en: It's an episode that I remember very well from the Lady Bird book about Henry V that I read as a little boy.
sentences.zh: 这个情节我印象非常深刻，因为我小时候读过一本关于亨利五世的瓢虫图书。

sentences.en: Yes, great illustration of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，里面的插图棒极了。

sentences.en: So Henry V has sent an embassy to France to basically demand his ancestral rights.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利五世派了一个使团去法国，主要为了索取他的祖传权力。

sentences.en: And the Dauphin replies to him by sending him this, in the Lady Bird book, there's a huge sort of chest full of tennis balls.
sentences.zh: 而王太子的回复是送给他一个东西，在瓢虫图书里，那是一个装满网球的巨大箱子。

sentences.en: And they're all kind of, they're all bouncing all over the court.
sentences.zh: 它们全都在球场上到处弹跳。

sentences.en: And Henry says in the play, his jest will savour but of shallow wit when thousands weep more than did laugh at it.
sentences.zh: 亨利在剧中说道：当千百人痛哭，笑过的人寥寥无几，他的笑话便显得愚蠢浅薄。

sentences.en: In other words, basically the Dauphin has said, this is, you know, why don't you play tennis and shut up and forget about interfering with France.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，王太子基本上是说，这，你知道的，你怎么不去打网球，闭上嘴，别管法国的闲事。

sentences.en: And Henry is very offended by this and is like, you won't be laughing.
sentences.zh: 亨利对此感到非常被冒犯，并说：你们笑不出来的。

sentences.en: When we turn up with our rackets and we will play such a set that men will, you know, or something like that.

sentences.zh: 这总是让我想起奥巴马嘲笑特朗普。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: At that, whatever it is, they hold the big thing for journalists.
sentences.zh: 在那个什么大会上，他们为记者们举办的大型活动。

sentences.en: Yeah, the thing with the journalists.
sentences.zh: 对，就是那个有记者的活动。

sentences.en: Presidents make terrible jokes and journalists pretend to find them amusing.
sentences.zh: 总统们讲着糟糕的笑话，记者们假装觉得很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Trump glowering and then goes off and kind of does a Henry V.
sentences.zh: 然后特朗普面色阴沉，随后离去，上演了一出“亨利五世”式的戏码。

sentences.en: So, I mean, the obvious question, did it actually happen?
sentences.zh: 所以，显而易见的问题是，这真的发生过吗？

sentences.en: So, Anne Currie, who is, as well as being a herald, is also the great doyenne of Agincourt studies.
sentences.zh: 因此，安·柯里，她不仅是一位纹章官，也是阿金库尔研究领域的泰斗。

sentences.en: She's a herald.
sentences.zh: 她是一位纹章官。

sentences.en: She's a herald.
sentences.zh: 她是一位纹章官。
