sentences.zh: 我想她是阿伦德尔伯爵的纹章官之类的。

sentences.en: When the Earl of Arundel goes out for dinner or something, does she accompany him in a surcoat, like blowing a trumpet?
sentences.zh: 当阿伦德尔伯爵出去吃晚饭时，她会穿着一件纹章大衣陪着他，像吹号角一样吗？

sentences.en: There's brilliant photographs of her in a kind of herald outfit.
sentences.zh: 有她穿着某种纹章服装的出色照片。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So check them out.
sentences.zh: 所以去看看吧。

sentences.en: So she's very sceptical.
sentences.zh: 所以她非常怀疑。

sentences.en: She says the whole story is easily dismissed.
sentences.zh: 她说整个故事完全不值一提。

sentences.en: But I'm pleased to say that Christopher Ormond, who's the great biographer of Henry V, he is slightly less sceptical.
sentences.zh: 不过我很高兴地说，亨利五世的伟大传记作家克里斯托弗·奥蒙德（Christopher Ormond）对此稍微没那么怀疑。

sentences.en: And he cites an Englishman who's gone on an embassy to Paris and is told by one of the Frenchmen opposite that they view Henry with utter contempt and his ambitions.
sentences.zh: 他引用了一个去巴黎出使的英国人的话，这人被对面的一名法国人告知，他们对亨利及其野心抱有极度的蔑视。

sentences.en: And that they're going to send him balls with which to play with and cushions upon which to lie.
sentences.zh: 而且他们打算送给他用来玩耍的球和供他躺卧的软垫。

sentences.en: And the implication is that essentially the king is a baby.
sentences.zh: 其暗示的意思基本上就是这位国王不过是个婴儿。

sentences.en: You know, this is all ridiculous talk.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些全都是荒谬的言论。

sentences.en: And so Ormond says, perhaps this is what kind of gave rise to the story.
sentences.zh: 所以奥蒙德说，也许正是这种事催生了这个故事。

sentences.en: And also, of course, it reflects the character of the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，这也反映了王太子的性格。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing that perhaps that he would do.
sentences.zh: 这正是他可能会做出的那种事。

sentences.en: But what it also does, it absolutely exemplifies the state of Anglo-French relations in the first two years of Henry V's reign.
sentences.zh: 但它同时做到的，是彻底展现了亨利五世统治前两年英法关系的状况。

sentences.en: Because essentially the story of these years is Henry sending embassies to Paris or to Burgundy to try and negotiate alliances or to extort lands and titles from the French king.
sentences.zh: 因为这些年来的故事本质上就是亨利派遣使团前往巴黎或勃艮第，试图谈判结盟，或者向法国国王勒索土地和头衔。

sentences.en: And the French refusing to play ball.
sentences.zh: 而法国人却拒绝配合。

sentences.en: So among the ambassadors who go is the son of Geoffrey Chaucer, Thomas Chaucer, who is Member of Parliament, Speaker for three times.
sentences.zh: 所以在出发的大使中，有杰弗里·乔叟的儿子托马斯·乔叟，他曾是国会议员、三次担任议长。

sentences.en: And he's going off to Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 他正前往勃艮第。

sentences.en: Others are going to Paris.
sentences.zh: 其他人则前往巴黎。

sentences.en: And they're demanding, first of all, a daughter of John the Fearless for Henry.
sentences.zh: 他们首先要求无畏者约翰的一个女儿嫁给亨利。

sentences.en: Then Catherine, the daughter of Charles VI.
sentences.zh: 然后是查理六世的女儿凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: They want all the lands that Edward III had been promised.
sentences.zh: 他们想要爱德华三世曾被承诺过的一切土地。

sentences.en: And also they'd quite like the Duchy of Normandy, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 而且他们或许还挺想要诺曼底公国。

sentences.en: And perhaps the throne of France.
sentences.zh: 或许还有法兰西的王位。

sentences.en: You know, it's unclear exactly what.
sentences.zh: 你知道，具体是什么并不清楚。

sentences.en: But basically they want lots of things.
sentences.zh: 但基本上他们想要很多东西。

sentences.en: And also they would like the full ransom that was supposed to have been paid for John, the king of France,
sentences.zh: 而且他们还想要原本应该为法国国王约翰支付的全部赎金，

sentences.en: who had been captured by the Black Prince at the Battle of Poitiers, in which the French had ended up not paying in its entirety.
sentences.zh: 约翰曾在普瓦捷战役中被黑太子俘虏，而法国人最终并没有全额支付这笔赎金。

sentences.en: But do you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: Henry V is the thing about like, oh, you're untried.
sentences.zh: 关于亨利五世，人们就像是说，哦，你还未经历过考验。

sentences.en: You're just a toddler.
sentences.zh: 你只是个蹒跚学步的幼儿。

sentences.en: Here are some tennis balls.
sentences.zh: 这儿有些网球。

sentences.en: You do the ludicrous demands.
sentences.zh: 你去提那些荒唐的要求吧。

sentences.en: Henry V is not a person to take lightly.
sentences.zh: 亨利五世可不是一个能被轻视的人。

sentences.en: No, exactly.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.en: Because as you said, he's 26 years old.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，他才26岁。

sentences.en: He's battle-hardened.
sentences.zh: 他身经百战。

sentences.en: And he's clearly a very sort of severe, serious, formidable man.
sentences.zh: 而且他显然是一个非常严厉、严肃、令人敬畏的人。

sentences.en: Seems to me bonkers that the Dauphin would have provoked him in this way.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，王太子用这种方式挑衅他简直是疯了。

sentences.en: And you know, Dominic, there are people in France who are keeping abreast of English affairs who do think Henry V is very impressive.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，多米尼克，法国国内有一些密切关注英国事务的人，他们确实觉得亨利五世非常了不起。

sentences.en: And not just as a soldier, but as a man who essentially he seems to have vowed celibacy until he gets married.
sentences.zh: 不仅作为一个军人，而且作为一个似乎发誓在结婚前保持独身的男人。

sentences.en: And the contrast there with the Dauphin is very great.
sentences.zh: 他与王太子形成了非常巨大的反差。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: He devotes himself full-bloodedly to all his responsibilities as king.
sentences.zh: 他全心全意地履行着作为国王的所有职责。

sentences.en: Again, huge contrast with the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 同样，与王太子形成了巨大的反差。

sentences.en: So there are people who actually quite admire him and are nervous about this.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有人相当崇拜他，并对此感到紧张。

sentences.en: And I think also what makes it all the stranger, you know, if the tennis balls thing did happen, is that France in this period, so in the years that follow Henry's coronation,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果网球的事情真的发生了，让这一切显得更加奇怪的是，这一时期的法国，也就是亨利加冕后的几年里，

sentences.en: is slipping right back into civil war.
sentences.zh: 正在迅速滑回内战。

sentences.en: So there'd been that brief compact between the Armagnacs and the Burgundians, which had seen the Duke of Clarence return with all his booty.
sentences.zh: 所以当时阿马尼亚克派和勃艮第派之间曾有过短暂的协议，克拉伦斯公爵带着他所有的战利品返回就是那时的结果。

sentences.en: But it doesn't laSt.
sentences.zh: 但好景不长。

sentences.en: And so in the same year that Henry is crowned, 1413,
sentences.zh: 因此，在亨利加冕的同一年，即1413年，

sentences.en: John the Fearless has been busy recruiting a paramilitary force with which to seize control of Paris.
sentences.zh: 无畏者约翰一直在忙于招募一支准军事部队，以夺取对巴黎的控制权。

sentences.en: And we're recording this in the wake of the series that we did on the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们是在录制完关于法国大革命的系列节目之后录制这一期的。

sentences.en: And there are some very weird premonitions of the French Revolution in this story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里有一些非常诡异的法国大革命预兆。

sentences.en: It's almost like a kind of overture.
sentences.zh: 它几乎就像是一种序曲。

sentences.en: So the people that John the Fearless is siding with are members of the Butcher's Guild in Paris, who are known as the Écocheurs.
sentences.zh: 所以无畏者约翰所支持的人是巴黎屠夫行会的成员，被称为剥皮者。

sentences.en: The Flairs.
sentences.zh: 剥皮者。

sentences.en: The Flairs, yes.
sentences.zh: 剥皮者，是的。

sentences.en: Or they're alternatively known as the Cabochien, after their leader, Simon Caboch.
sentences.zh: 或者他们也被称作卡博申派，是以他们的领袖西蒙·卡博命名。

sentences.en: And they wear very distinctive white hoods.
sentences.zh: 他们戴着非常独特的白色兜帽。

sentences.en: And it's a bit like the Liberty Cap.
sentences.zh: 这有点像自由之帽。

sentences.en: They basically go around forcing their superiors to wear these caps as a way of kind of humbling them.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上四处强迫他们的上级戴上这些帽子，以此来羞辱他们。

sentences.en: So they force them on noblemans.
sentences.zh: 所以他们强迫贵族戴上。

sentences.en: They force them on clerics and bishops.
sentences.zh: 他们强迫神职人员和主教戴上。

sentences.en: And they even force them on the Queen's Ladies of Honor.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至强迫王后的女官们戴上。

sentences.en: And they commission investigators to go around the city, finding out people whose hearts are not fully with them,
sentences.zh: 他们还委托调查人员在城里四处搜查，找出那些内心并不完全忠于他们的人，

sentences.en: who are not engaged with this kind of revolution that they're trying to instill.
sentences.zh: 那些没有参与他们试图灌输的这种革命的人。

sentences.en: And then the names of those who are not on the side of the Cabochien are proclaimed at street corners.
sentences.zh: 然后，那些不支持卡博申派的人的名字会在街头巷尾被宣读出来。

sentences.en: So there is a kind of slight 1791 quality to all this, except that they are not targeting the king.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切多少带有一点1791年的特质，只不过他们的目标不是国王。

sentences.en: And there are opportunities for John the Fearless to exploit them.
sentences.zh: 而且这也给无畏者约翰提供了利用他们的机会。

sentences.en: And that's what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是他正在做的事。

sentences.en: Because basically he's using them to intimidate the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上是在利用他们来恐吓王太子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And at the beginning of May 1413, the Cabochien invade the Dauphin's palace.
sentences.zh: 在1413年5月初，卡博申派侵入了王太子的宫殿。

sentences.en: They've brought in a white hood.
sentences.zh: 他们带进了一个白色兜帽。

sentences.en: They make the Dauphin wear it.
sentences.zh: 他们强迫王太子戴上它。

sentences.en: And the Cabochien kind of give him a stern lecture, say, you're rubbish.
sentences.zh: 并且卡博申派严厉训斥了他一番，说你太差劲了。

sentences.en: You know, you need to pull your socks up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你需要振作起来。

sentences.en: They bring in clerics who give the poor Dauphin kind of lots of sermons, tell him to pull his socks up.
sentences.zh: 他们找来神职人员对可怜的王太子进行了一大堆说教，告诉他要振作起来。

sentences.en: And they also attack and eliminate a lot of the Dauphin's particular allies.
sentences.zh: 他们还袭击并清除许多王太子的亲信。

sentences.en: So Anne Curry, in her absolutely groundbreaking book on Agincourt, she says that their assaults included the public beheading of the corpse of the Dauphin's chamberlain,
sentences.zh: 因此，安·柯里在她那本关于阿让库尔的开创性著作中写道，他们的袭击包括公开斩首王太子侍臣的尸体，

sentences.en: who had allegedly committed suicide in prison by hitting his head repeatedly with a wine jug.
sentences.zh: 而此人据称此前在狱中用酒壶多次猛击自己的头部来自杀身亡。

sentences.en: I saw that and I was sceptical.
sentences.zh: 我看到这时持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Would that work?
sentences.zh: 这行得通吗？

sentences.en: If you just hit yourself again and again with that jug?
sentences.zh: 如果你用那个壶一遍又一遍地砸自己？

sentences.en: I don't think that would work.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这行不通。

sentences.en: No, of course not.
sentences.zh: 不，当然行不通。

sentences.en: It's a deliberate way of saying, you know, we're not admitting to the murder, but basically we will murder you.
sentences.zh: 这是一种故意的表态，你知道的，我们不承认谋杀，但基本上我们会谋杀了你。

sentences.en: So he was definitely killed by these white hooded Cabochien?
sentences.zh: 所以他绝对是被这些戴白兜帽的卡博申派杀害的？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: The Flayers.
sentences.zh: 剥皮者。

sentences.en: This is very Game of Thrones territory here.
sentences.zh: 这非常具有《权力的游戏》的风格。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes, and maybe not coincidentally.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且或许并非巧合。

sentences.en: I mean, I think all this period is kind of huge influence on the writing of Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这段历史对《权力的游戏》的创作有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so the poor Dauphin ends up basically a kind of prisoner.
sentences.zh: 因此，可怜的王太子最终基本上变成了一种人质。

sentences.en: The king all this while has been, you know, he's been out with his mental probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而国王这段时间以来一直，你知道的，一直受精神问题困扰。

sentences.en: Then he recovers from them.
sentences.zh: 然后他从病中恢复。

sentences.en: He goes in a state procession to Notre Dame to give thanks.
sentences.zh: 他举行国家游行前往巴黎圣母院谢恩。

sentences.en: And the Cabochien ambush him.
sentences.zh: 结果卡博申派伏击了他。

sentences.en: And inevitably, they've got a white hood and they make the king wear it.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，他们准备了一个白色兜帽，并强迫国王戴上。

sentences.en: And the king puts it on.
sentences.zh: 国王戴上了它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So very bad.
sentences.zh: 情况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And the king and the Dauphin between them think, well, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 国王和王太子商量后认为，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, we need to sort this out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们得解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And so they turn to the Armagnacs who are lurking off in Orléans.
sentences.zh: 于是他们向盘踞在奥尔良的阿马尼亚克派求助。

sentences.en: And most of the Armagnacs are too nervous to intervene because they're afraid of the Cabochien.
sentences.zh: 而大部分阿马尼亚克派都太紧张而不敢介入，因为他们害怕卡博申派。

sentences.en: They're, you know, they're very, very menacing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们非常非常具有威胁性。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: But there is the Count of Alençon, who you may remember we described as this kind of fearless, bold, boar-like man.
sentences.zh: 但还有阿朗松伯爵，你可能还记得我们曾将他描述为那种无畏、大胆、如野猪般的男人。

sentences.en: A bruiser, you said he was.
sentences.zh: 你曾说他是个恶霸硬汉。

sentences.en: A bruiser.
sentences.zh: 一个恶霸。

sentences.en: And he's not having, you know, he's not going to be intimidated by a bunch of butchers.
sentences.zh: 而且他可不买账，你知道的，他不会被一群屠夫吓倒。

sentences.en: So he raises a force, coordinates an attack on Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以他召集了一支军队，策划了对巴黎的进攻。

sentences.en: And on the 4th of August, 1413, the Armagnacs break into Paris and they massacre the Cabochien, who prove unable to deal with armed knights who have burst into the city.
sentences.zh: 在1413年8月4日，阿马尼亚克派冲进巴黎并大肆屠杀卡博申派，这些屠夫根本无力应对冲进城中的武装骑士。

sentences.en: John the Fearless, you know, all his plans are falling to pieces.
sentences.zh: 无畏者约翰的计划，你知道的，全都泡汤了。

sentences.en: He tries to kidnap the king.
sentences.zh: 他试图绑架国王。

sentences.en: That's frustrated.
sentences.zh: 但没有成功。

sentences.en: He then scarpers.
sentences.zh: 随后他溜之大吉。

sentences.en: And, of course, this is brilliant for the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对阿马尼亚克派来说太棒了。

sentences.en: They've now got Paris.
sentences.zh: 他们现在占领了巴黎。

sentences.en: They've got the king.
sentences.zh: 他们控制了国王。

sentences.en: But it's still not brilliant for the Dauphin because now he's replaced the Burgundians with the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 但对王太子来说依然不算太妙，因为他现在只是把勃艮第派换成了阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they're still kind of kicking him around.
sentences.zh: 而且他们依然在欺负他。

sentences.en: Basically, you know, he wants to be the big man.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你知道的，他想成为大人物。

sentences.en: He wants to be in charge.
sentences.zh: 他想掌权。

sentences.en: But it's always either the Burgundians or the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 但掌权的总是勃艮第派或者阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: And the Dauphin and the king remain essentially ciphers.
sentences.zh: 王太子和国王本质上依然只是傀儡。

sentences.en: And so instead of a return to a secure monarchy, there's a collapse back into civil war.
sentences.zh: 因此，非但没有回到稳定的君主制，反而再次陷入了内战的崩溃中。

sentences.en: John the Fearless is banished from France as a traitor.
sentences.zh: 无畏者约翰作为叛徒被驱逐出法兰西。

sentences.en: The Armagnacs march into Burgundian territories.
sentences.zh: 阿马尼亚克派大举进军勃艮第领地。

sentences.en: They attack the town of Soissons, which is a Burgundian town.
sentences.zh: 他们进攻了属于勃艮第派的城镇苏瓦松。

sentences.en: They storm it and they inflict a brutal, notorious storm on it.
sentences.zh: 他们攻占了该城，并对其实施了残酷而臭名昭著的强攻。

sentences.en: The town is wasted.
sentences.zh: 全城被毁。

sentences.en: Nuns are raped.
sentences.zh: 修女遭到强奸。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So while all this is going on, presumably Henry V is in England and he's watching all this.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一切发生的同时，亨利五世大概正身在英国注视着这一切。

sentences.en: And he must be thinking, as France slips further and further into chaos, this is my opportunity.
sentences.zh: 随着法兰西进一步陷入混乱，他心里一定在想，这就是我的机会。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the prize waiting for the plucking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，胜利的果实就等著去摘取了。

sentences.en: He does absolutely think that.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是这么想的。

sentences.en: And so he starts sending renewed embassies to John the Fearless saying, you know, come on, let's have an alliance.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始重新向无畏者约翰派遣使团，说，你知道的，来吧，我们结盟吧。

sentences.en: Let's go and attack Paris and the Armagnacs together.
sentences.zh: 让我们一起去攻打巴黎和阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: But John the Fearless is also a very shrewd political player.
sentences.zh: 但无畏者约翰也是个非常精明的政治玩家。

sentences.en: And so he uses the threat of an English alliance essentially to kind of force a peace on the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 因此他利用与英国结盟的威胁，基本上迫使阿马尼亚克派求和。

sentences.en: And so they sign yet another compact.
sentences.zh: 于是他们又签署了一项协议。

sentences.en: And this is very bad news for Henry because suddenly, you know, he no longer has a potential alliance with the Burgundians.
sentences.zh: 这对亨利来说是个极其糟糕的消息，因为突然之间，你知道的，他不再拥有与勃艮第派结盟的可能了。

sentences.en: And Henry's ambassadors, who are actually in Paris when this Armagnac-Burgundian peace is announced, realize that the ground has been completely cut from under their feet.
sentences.zh: 而亨利的大使们当时正好在巴黎，当阿马尼亚克与勃艮第媾和的消息宣布时，他们意识到自己的立足点被彻底抽空了。

sentences.en: They leave Paris empty-handed.
sentences.zh: 他们空手离开巴黎。

sentences.en: They travel back, Dominic, to the Normandy coaSt.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他们踏上了返回诺曼底海岸的旅程。

sentences.en: And they take ship for England from the port of Harfleur.
sentences.zh: 并在1415年3月底前从哈夫勒尔港乘船返回英国。

sentences.en: And they're back by the end of March 1415 with nothing to show for their diplomatic efforts, seemingly humiliated.
sentences.zh: 他们的外交努力毫无成果，看起来备受羞辱。

sentences.en: But Henry, he's not bothered about that, right?
sentences.zh: 不过亨利对此并不介意，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he has already made his mind up that actually, you know, he'll never get a better opportunity to carve out more lands, also to improve his reputation.
sentences.zh: 因为他心里已经打定主意，事实上，你懂的，他觉得再也找不到比这更好的机会来开疆拓土、提升声望了。

sentences.en: You know, there are all kinds of reasons pushing him in favour of the French war, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有各种各样的原因促使他赞成对法兰克开战，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so he's basically decided since the beginning of 1415 that he is going to go to war no matter what happens in Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上从1415年初就决定了，无论巴黎发生什么，他都要开战。

sentences.en: So at the end of January, he'd assembled representatives from all the kind of the main ports and harbours of southern England to tell them,
sentences.zh: 因此在1月下旬，他召集了英格兰南部各大港口和海湾的代表，对他们说，

sentences.en: I need ships, you know, provide me with ships.
sentences.zh: 我需要船，你们知道的，给我提供船。

sentences.en: He'd start putting out feelers to Hanseatic ports along the coast of northern Europe.
sentences.zh: 他开始向欧洲北部海岸的汉萨同盟港口探听口风。

sentences.en: 20th of February, he has sent out summons to a great council of all the peers of England, which is due to meet on the 15th of April.
sentences.zh: 2月20日，他向英格兰全体贵族发出大议会传唤令，定于4月15日开会。

sentences.en: And now, just before that meeting, his ambassadors come back from Paris, seemingly humiliated.
sentences.zh: 现在，就在这次会议召开前夕，他的大使从巴黎回来了，看起来受到了羞辱。

sentences.en: And so he can demonstrate to the English and to the whole of Christendom that, you know, he's tried, he's made efforts and his peace-loving efforts have been rebuffed.
sentences.zh: 这样他就可以向英格兰人乃至整个基督教世界证明，你知道的，他已经尽力了，他做出了努力，但他爱好和平的努力遭到了拒绝。

sentences.en: So that's why the tennis ball story works.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么网球的故事讲得通。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because the tennis ball story, I mean, it can stand in for him saying, look, I've asked, I've asked nicely, I've pursued the path of diplomacy and it has failed.
sentences.zh: 因为网球的故事，我的意思是，它可以代表他说：看吧，我问过了，我客客气气地问过了，我一直在追求外交途径，但失败了。

sentences.en: They've been thrown back in my face.
sentences.zh: 他们把我的好意狠狠地甩回了脸上。

sentences.en: I have no alternative now but to take military action.
sentences.zh: 现在我别无选择，只能采取军事行动。

sentences.en: Because, you know, the mockery of Henry is the mockery of England.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，对亨利的嘲弄就是对英格兰的嘲弄。

sentences.en: And so everyone in England, and including Parliament, crucially, which votes money, can now be expected to rally behind him.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰的每一个人，至关重要的是包括掌握财政拨款权的议会在内，现在都可以预料到会团结在他身后。

sentences.en: So it's an absolutely classic example of Henry's genius, which he demonstrates throughout his life.
sentences.zh: 因此，这绝对是亨利一生中展现的天才的经典范例。

sentences.en: He can turn seeming rebuffs, seeming setbacks, seeming disasters to his own advantage.
sentences.zh: 他能把看似的拒绝、看似的挫折、看似的灾难转化为自己的优势。

sentences.en: And he will do this throughout his forthcoming invasion of France.
sentences.zh: 而且他在即将到来的对法兰克入侵中也会这样做。

sentences.en: But I guess it does focus one obvious question that people listening may have been wondering, which is, apart from expediency,
sentences.zh: 但我想这确实引出了听众可能会好奇的一个显而易见的问题，那就是，除了功利考量，

sentences.en: apart from the opportunity that the civil war in France offers him, you know, are there other motives he has for going to war?
sentences.zh: 除了法兰克国内内战为他提供的机会，你知道的，他发动战争还有其他动机吗？

sentences.en: And I think indisputably, he authentically and genuinely believes that God does want him to be king.
sentences.zh: 我想毫无疑问，他真诚而笃信上帝希望他成为国王。

sentences.en: So, to quote Jonathan Sumption, who's written this absolutely enormous history of the Hundred Years' War in Cursed Kings, his book on this period, Sumption writes,
sentences.zh: 因此，引用乔纳森·萨姆森的话——他在这本关于这段时期的著作《被诅咒的国王》中写下了这部极其宏大的百年战争史，萨姆森写道，

sentences.en: Henry constantly presented his claims against the French as an appeal to God, against the wickedness and unworthiness of England's traditional enemy.
sentences.zh: 亨利不断地将他对法兰克的诉求表现为对上帝的呼吁，以此对抗英格兰传统敌人邪恶且不配的行径。

sentences.en: And Sumption goes on to say, this is not humbug.
sentences.zh: 萨姆森接着说，这不是虚伪。

sentences.en: Henry is a ferociously devout and orthodox king, and he absolutely believes it.
sentences.zh: 亨利是一位极其虔诚且恪守正统的国王，他对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: He genuinely thinks he has a right to be the king of France, and that goes back to Edward III, and he thinks this isn't just propaganda, it's not, you know, contrivance,
sentences.zh: 他真心认为自己有权成为法兰克国王，这可以追溯到爱德华三世，他认为这不仅仅是宣传，不是，你知道的，虚构，

sentences.en: it's not an excuse, it's real.
sentences.zh: 也不是借口，这是真的。

sentences.en: I should be the king of France, and God wants me to be the king of France.
sentences.zh: 我应当成为法兰克国王，上帝希望我成为法兰克国王。

sentences.en: I think his readiness to invade France shows that he does think that, because effectively for Henry, devout that he is, by invading France, he is putting himself to the teSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为他准备入侵法兰克的行动表明他确实是这么想的，因为对虔诚的亨利而言，通过入侵法兰克，他正在接受考验。

sentences.en: And if he fails, then it will demonstrate that God is not on his side.
sentences.zh: 如果他失败了，那就证明上帝并不站在他这一边。

sentences.en: If he succeeds, then it will demonstrate that God is on his side.
sentences.zh: 如果他成功了，那就证明上帝站在他这一边。

sentences.en: But, Tom, more prosaically, if he invades France, if he gets Parliament to vote in money, he invades France, he goes horribly wrong, he could be killed, he could be taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，更现实地说，如果他入侵法兰克，如果他让议会投票通过拨款，他入侵法兰克，结果一败涂地，他可能会被杀，可能会被俘虏。

sentences.en: But also, it could shatter his legitimacy back at home, right?
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也可能粉碎他在国内的合法性，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, listeners won't have forgotten, his father was a usurper.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听众不会忘记，他的父亲是个篡位者。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, he's a usurper himself, you could argue, or at least he's the beneficiary of a usurpation.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，你也可以说他自己就是一个篡位者，或者至少他是篡位行为的受益者。

sentences.en: And so, his legitimacy is more precious and also more fragile than it would be if he were a different king.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的合法性比换作其他国王时更加珍贵，同时也更加脆弱。

sentences.en: Well, I think this is a further dimension, because it is often the way of the very devout, that they tend to devoutly believe things that they need to believe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是另一个维度，因为这往往是极其虔诚之人的行事方式，他们往往会虔诚地相信那些他们需要相信的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this idea that Henry V, who is the son of a usurper, might be able to consolidate his regime and rally his people behind him,
sentences.zh: 而这个想法，即作为篡位者之子的亨利五世，也许能够巩固他的政权并把人民团结在自己身后，

sentences.en: is summed up in a phrase that Shakespeare uses in Henry IV, where the dying king is talking to his son and offering him his advice for how he should rule.
sentences.zh: 在莎士比亚在《亨利四世》中使用的一句话中得到了总结，剧中垂死的国王正在与他的儿子交谈，并向他提出如何统治的建议。

sentences.en: And he says, busy, giddy minds with foreign quarrels.
sentences.zh: 他说，用对外争端来占据那些晕头转向之人的心智。

sentences.en: In other words, take the minds of people in England off rebellion against you, off insurrection, and channel those energies into war with France.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，让英格兰人民的心思从反叛你、从暴动中转移开，并将这些精力引导到与法兰克的战争中。

sentences.en: And Henry is undoubtedly very, very aware of the fact that he's the son of a usurper.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，亨利非常非常清楚自己是篡位者的儿子这一事实。

sentences.en: So, Henry IV had buried Richard II's body, not in Westminster Abbey in the great tomb that Richard II had prepared for himself.
sentences.zh: 所以，亨利四世安葬理查二世的遗体时，没有将其安葬在威斯敏斯特大教堂理查二世为自己准备的宏伟陵墓中。

sentences.en: But Henry V has Richard II's body translated to that tomb.
sentences.zh: 但亨利五世却将理查二世的遗体迁到了那个陵墓。

sentences.en: And I think that that reflects the fact, again, that Henry V is a great believer in the sanctity of himself as an anointed king.
sentences.zh: 我认为这再次反映了一个事实，即亨利五世坚信自己作为受膏君王的圣洁性。

sentences.en: And so, he genuinely believes in the sanctity of Richard II as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，他也真诚地相信理查二世的圣洁性。

sentences.en: So, there are all kinds of complicated motives.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面有各种复杂的动机。

sentences.en: But I do agree, Henry is laying things on the line, because essentially, if he fails, it will not only prove that God is not on his side,
sentences.zh: 但我确实同意，亨利是在孤注一掷，因为本质上，如果他失败了，这不仅会证明上帝不站在他这一边，

sentences.en: but it may well shatter his reign and the whole legitimacy of the Lancastrian dynasty for good.
sentences.zh: 而且很可能会彻底粉碎他的统治以及兰开斯特王朝的全部合法性。

sentences.en: So, the stakes are absolutely enormous.
sentences.zh: 所以，赌注绝对是巨大的。

sentences.en: But I think, you know, he's relying on God's backing for him, but he's also relying on the fact that France is in chaos, and that he himself, as king, is a seasoned leader,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，你知道的，他依靠上帝对他的支持，但他也依靠法兰克陷入混乱这一事实，以及他自己作为国王是一位经验丰富的领袖，

sentences.en: and that he is qualified, absolutely, to lead an invasion.
sentences.zh: 并且他完全有资格领导一场入侵。

sentences.en: He's only been king for two years.
sentences.zh: 他当国王才两年。

sentences.en: There's only two years, aren't there, between him becoming king and Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 从他当上国王到阿金库尔战役，只有短短两年时间，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Why the urgency?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么急迫？

sentences.en: I mean, he's 26.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他才26岁。

sentences.en: He could be king for another quarter of a century, you know, if not longer.
sentences.zh: 他还可以再当四分之一个世纪的国王，你知道的，甚至更久。

sentences.en: So, why does he feel, of course, France is a bit of a basket case right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么他觉得——当然，法兰克现在有点像个烂摊子。

sentences.en: But do you think that speaks to a deep insecurity, that he feels he has to prove himself quickly?
sentences.zh: 但你认为这说明了一种深层的缺乏安全感，让他觉得必须尽快证明自己吗？

sentences.en: I mean, to put it all on the line straight away when you're 26 years old?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在你26岁的时候，直接把一切都押上去？

sentences.en: I think that is part of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是原因之一。

sentences.en: But I think, above all, he just feels, you know, he's going to be good at it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最重要的是，他只是觉得自己，你知道的，他会擅长这事。

sentences.en: He's going to do it.
sentences.zh: 他能把它办成。

sentences.en: And you will know, because we've discussed this, that I once nominated Henry V as the most overrated king in English history.
sentences.zh: 你会知道的，因为我们讨论过，我曾经提名亨利五世为英格兰历史上被高估最多的国王。

sentences.en: Because I thought that launching an invasion of France, that it was doomed ultimately to failure, that it was a waste of resources.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为对法兰克发动入侵最终注定会失败，这是对资源的浪费。

sentences.en: That it was a kind of ultimately an immoral thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这在本质上是一种不道德的行为。

sentences.en: Having gone deep into this, I've now slightly changed my mind on that.
sentences.zh: 在深入了解之后，我现在对此略有改变看法。

sentences.en: I still think that it was, you know, it proves to be a terrible waste of money and resources and inflicts devastation on large numbers of people.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为，你知道的，事实证明这是一场对金钱和资源的糟糕浪费，并给大量人民带来了毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: You know, horrific for France.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对法兰克来说太可怕了。

sentences.en: But I think to blame Henry for doing it is kind of akin to blaming, I don't know, a lion for eating a zebra.
sentences.zh: 但我认为把这归咎于亨利，有点类似于指责，我不知道，指责一头狮子吃斑马。

sentences.en: It's just what he's going to do.
sentences.zh: 这只是他要做的事。

sentences.en: He is a great king.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的国王。

sentences.en: He's a formidable military operator.
sentences.zh: 他是一位令人生畏的军事统帅。

sentences.en: He has the opportunity.
sentences.zh: 他有这个机会。

sentences.en: He thinks God is on his side.
sentences.zh: 他认为上帝站在他这一边。

sentences.en: Why wait?
sentences.zh: 为什么还要等？

sentences.en: Let's crack on.
sentences.zh: 我们大干一场吧。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: And Henry can be confident that he'll be successful because he can trust not just in his own abilities, but he also, I mean,
sentences.zh: 亨利可以确信他会成功，因为他不仅可以信任自己的能力，而且我还想说，

sentences.en: he's very much on top of all the other advantages he has.
sentences.zh: 他非常清楚自己拥有的所有其他优势。

sentences.en: So, I mean, just to look at them, he has hugely experienced lieutenants.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，仅从这些来看，他拥有经验极其丰富的副将。

sentences.en: So he has his three brothers.
sentences.zh: 所以他有他的三个兄弟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's got Clarence, who's already been on an expedition.
sentences.zh: 所以他有克拉伦斯，他已经参加过一次远征了。

sentences.en: He's got his younger brother, Humphrey, the Duke of Gloucester, who will be going with him on the expedition and being kind of blooded on this campaign.
sentences.zh: 他有他的弟弟汉弗莱，格洛斯特公爵，他将随他一起参加远征，并在这场战役中经受洗礼。

sentences.en: He's going to leave his middle brother, John, the Duke of Bedford, behind.
sentences.zh: 他将把他的二哥约翰，贝德福德公爵留在后方。

sentences.en: Very competent, very loyal again.
sentences.zh: 非常能干，同样非常忠诚。

sentences.en: So Henry can be sure that England is secure in his rear.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利可以确信后方的英格兰安然无恙。

sentences.en: He's got his broader family.
sentences.zh: 他有更广的家族成员。

sentences.en: So notably, Edward, the Duke of York, his cousin, who will be a kind of prominent leader on the campaign that's coming up.
sentences.zh: 最值得注意的是爱德华，约克公爵，他的表弟，他将成为即将到来的战役中的主要将领。

sentences.en: He's got his friends.
sentences.zh: 他有他的朋友们。

sentences.en: He's got the Earl of Arundel, who led the campaign in 1411.
sentences.zh: 他有阿伦黛尔伯爵，他曾率领1411年的战役。

sentences.en: And he's the bloke who's got Anne Currie, the historian, as his herald.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个让历史学家安·柯里担任其纹章官的家伙。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: It all interweaves.
sentences.zh: 这一切都交织在一起。

sentences.en: So Henry's got Arundel and he's got all the rest of the peers.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利有阿伦黛尔，还有其他所有的贵族。

sentences.en: And basically, all the peers will be coming with him.
sentences.zh: 基本上，所有的贵族都会跟他一起去。

sentences.en: Henry's expecting that.
sentences.zh: 亨利对此充满期待。

sentences.en: But they want to go.
sentences.zh: 但他们自己也想去。

sentences.en: I mean, Henry is giving them what Edward III had given them and which Richard II hadn't, which is an opportunity for loot and glory and basically fun.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，亨利正在给予他们爱德华三世曾给予他们而理查二世没有给予他们的东西，那就是掠夺战利品、获得荣耀以及基本上寻欢作乐的机会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So they're all lined up behind him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都排队站在他身后。

sentences.en: You know, unlike the French nobles are all busy attacking each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不像法兰克的贵族们正忙着互相攻击。

sentences.en: The English nobles, they're ready to go.
sentences.zh: 英格兰的贵族们，他们已经准备好出发了。

sentences.en: And of course, Henry has, as he well knows, because he ended up with an arrow as a young man sticking in his skull.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如亨利自己很清楚的那样，因为他年轻时脑袋里曾插过一支箭。

sentences.en: He has the most lethal killing machine in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他拥有欧洲最具杀伤力的杀戮机器。

sentences.en: Massive contingents of longbowmen.
sentences.zh: 庞大的长弓手分队。

sentences.en: And just to remind people of what that means.
sentences.zh: 提醒大家一下这意味着什么。

sentences.en: These are arrows that can be fired with great accuracy, over 200 metres.
sentences.zh: 这些是能够以极高准确度发射、射程超过200米的箭矢。

sentences.en: A trained longbowman can fire kind of like 15 arrows a minute.
sentences.zh: 一个训练有素的长弓手一分钟能射出大约15支箭。

sentences.en: Henry's taking about 7,000 archers to France.
sentences.zh: 亨利带了大约7000名弓箭手去法兰克。

sentences.en: So 7,000 archers, they could fire, what, kind of over 100,000 arrows in a minute.
sentences.zh: 所以7000名弓箭手，他们一分钟能射出，什么，大约10万多支箭。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Collectively.
sentences.zh: 齐射。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a devastating firestorm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场毁灭性的火力风暴。

sentences.en: Henry knows what this is like.
sentences.zh: 亨利知道这是什么滋味。

sentences.en: He's suffered it.
sentences.zh: 他经历过。

sentences.en: He's experienced it.
sentences.zh: 他体验过。

sentences.en: And these archers, some of them are coming from Cheshire.
sentences.zh: 这些弓箭手，他们中有一些来自柴郡。

sentences.en: You know, Henry was the Earl of Chester as the Prince of Wales.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，亨利作为威尔士亲王曾担任过切斯特伯爵。

sentences.en: He knows how good they are.
sentences.zh: 他知道他们有多厉害。

sentences.en: There are archers from Wales as well, also from Lancashire.
sentences.zh: 还有来自威尔士的弓箭手，以及来自兰开夏郡的弓箭手。

sentences.en: These are the best in the country and therefore in the whole of Christendom.
sentences.zh: 这些是全国最好的，因而也是整个基督教世界最好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Speak to anybody from Wales about the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 跟任何来自威尔士的人聊聊中世纪吧。

sentences.en: If it ever comes up, they will tell you Welsh archers won the Battle of Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 如果谈到这个话题，他们会告诉你威尔士弓箭手赢得了阿金库尔战役。

sentences.en: That's what it's all about.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so these contingents exclusively consist of archers.
sentences.zh: 所以这些分队完全由弓箭手组成。

sentences.en: Because contingents that are coming from elsewhere tend to be mixed in with men-at-arMs.
sentences.zh: 因为从其他地方来的分队往往与重甲步兵混编。

sentences.en: And I think under Edward III, these contingents had been pretty much 50-50.
sentences.zh: 我想在爱德华三世时期，这些分队差不多是五五开。

sentences.en: But under Henry V, the archers tend to outnumber men-at-arms about three to one.
sentences.zh: 但在亨利五世时期，弓箭手与重甲步兵的比例往往达到大约三比一。

sentences.en: And I think that this reflects Henry's own decision.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了亨利自己的决定。

sentences.en: It's his innovation.
sentences.zh: 这是他的创新。

sentences.en: And he'd introduced it in Wales.
sentences.zh: 他在威尔士时就引入了这一点。

sentences.en: Maybe because he'd had that arrow, you know, he'd been shot.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为他挨过那一箭，你知道的，他曾被射中过。

sentences.en: It's kind of intensified for him his sense of just how dangerous this can be.
sentences.zh: 这让他更加深刻地意识到这会有多危险。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And therefore, how lethal.
sentences.zh: 因而也就是有多致命。

sentences.en: So Anne Currie's stats on this, of the expedition going to France, about 80% are archers, are longbowmen.
sentences.zh: 所以安·柯里关于这次去法兰克的远征的数据显示，大约80%是弓箭手，是长弓手。

sentences.en: So really, that's a gamble, though.
sentences.zh: 所以说，这确实是一场豪赌。

sentences.en: That is a gamble.
sentences.zh: 这是一场赌博。

sentences.en: Because if the enemy close in, those archers, you know, they're defenseless, basically against enemy knights or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为如果敌军逼近，那些弓箭手，你知道的，基本上毫无防备，无法抵挡敌方骑士之类的人。

sentences.en: It is a gamble.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场赌博。

sentences.en: But it's a gamble that reflects Henry's years of campaigning in Wales.
sentences.zh: 但这场赌博反映了亨利在威尔士多年的征战经验。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And also, the other thing, of course, that Henry learnt in Wales is the fact that you need money and you need the supplies that money can then buy.
sentences.zh: 而且，另一件当然是亨利在威尔士学到的事情，那就是你需要资金，以及资金能够买到的物资。

sentences.en: He, again, has lots of experience of this.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，他同样经验丰富。

sentences.en: And so he's got Parliament on board.
sentences.zh: 所以他得到了议会的支持。

sentences.en: So Thomas Chaucer, who we mentioned, he'd been three times Speaker.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到过的托马斯·乔叟，曾三次担任议长。

sentences.en: In November 1414, he'd become Speaker for a record fourth time.
sentences.zh: 在1414年11月，他第四次当选议长，创下了记录。

sentences.en: He raises a company.
sentences.zh: 他组建了一支队伍。

sentences.en: He's so enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 他表现得非常热情。

sentences.en: So he has 12 men-at-arms, 37 archers.
sentences.zh: 于是他拥有了12名重甲骑兵和37名弓箭手。

sentences.en: So, again, that's that one to three proportion.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，这就是一比三的比例。

sentences.en: Sadly, Thomas Chaucer is invalided out before he can leave.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，托马斯·乔叟在出发前因伤病退出了。

sentences.en: But the archers and men-at-arms go.
sentences.zh: 但弓箭手和重甲骑兵还是出发了。

sentences.en: But in better news, Dick Whittington is on board.
sentences.zh: 不过有个好消息，迪克·惠廷顿加入了。

sentences.en: Dick Whittington is on board.
sentences.zh: 迪克·惠廷顿加入了。

sentences.en: So he's the mayor of London.
sentences.zh: 他可是伦敦市长。

sentences.en: He's rallying behind.
sentences.zh: 他在后方全力支持。

sentences.en: Lots of loans.
sentences.zh: 筹集了大量贷款。

sentences.en: So it's all great.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: And so Henry, as a result, is able to raise certainly the largest force that had been mustered in England since the time of Edward III.
sentences.zh: 因此，亨利得以集结了自爱德华三世时代以来英格兰规模最大的一支军队。

sentences.en: Maybe 12,000 men.
This is a pretty formidable force.
sentences.zh: 这是一支相当强大的军队。

sentences.en: And his aim is a lot more than just a kind of cursory raid.
sentences.zh: 他的目标远不止是一次走过场式的突袭。

sentences.en: His immediate target is Harfleur, that nest of pirates.
sentences.zh: 他眼前的目标是哈弗勒尔，那个海盗巢穴。

sentences.en: If he can flush that out and take it, then that would be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 如果他能将其肃清并攻占，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: And maybe he could make it into a second Calais because the English hold Calais as a result of Edward III's wars.
sentences.zh: 也许他能把它变成第二个加来，因为英国人正是通过爱德华三世的战争占领了加来。

sentences.en: And if they can make Harfleur a second Calais, then that would be great.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能把哈弗勒尔变成第二个加来，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: But Harfleur, because it's in Normandy, can also serve him as a launch pad for his kind of more ambitious plan,
sentences.zh: 但哈弗勒尔位于诺曼底，也可以成为他实施更宏大计划的跳板，

sentences.en: which is essentially to reclaim the Duchy of Normandy that William the Conqueror and his heirs had held.
sentences.zh: 这个计划本质上是要收回征服者威廉及其继承人曾拥有过的诺曼底公国。

sentences.en: And he's clearly been preparing for this because when English ambassadors go to Paris, they've suddenly become quite keen on Henry's legal right to the Duchy of Normandy,
sentences.zh: 他显然一直在为此做准备，因为当英国大使前往巴黎时，他们突然对亨利对诺曼底公国的法律权利表现出极大的兴趣，

sentences.en: which had actually ceased to exist, you know, maybe 200 years before.
sentences.zh: 而这个公国实际上在两百年前就已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: And the French are quite puzzled by this.
sentences.zh: 法国人对此感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: I mean, they shouldn't have been.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们本不该感到困惑的。

sentences.en: It's pretty clear why Henry would be interested in that.
sentences.zh: 亨利为什么会对这个感兴趣，原因显而易见。

sentences.en: And on top of that, if you're going to take the very, very strongly fortified towns and castles of Normandy, you will need the latest weapon, which is cannon.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，如果你打算攻克诺曼底那些防御极其坚固的城镇和城堡，你就需要最新的武器，那就是大炮。

sentences.en: And Henry IV had been a big fan of cannon.
sentences.zh: 亨利四世曾是大炮的狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: He'd fired them at Berwick.
sentences.zh: 他曾在贝里克使用过大炮。

sentences.en: It was the first attack on a British city with cannon.
sentences.zh: 那是历史上首次用大炮攻击英国城市。

sentences.en: And Henry V has inherited that enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 亨利五世继承了这种热情。

sentences.en: And he's commissioned all sorts of cannon in the Tower of London and takes with him to France, the largest cannon ever forged in England.
sentences.zh: 他在伦敦塔定制了各种大炮，并把英格兰锻造过的最大火炮带到了法国。

sentences.en: So it's all looking absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以一切看起来都完美极了。

sentences.en: The invasion fleet is massing in the Solent, ready to cross to Normandy.
sentences.zh: 侵略舰队正在索伦特海峡集结，准备横渡前往诺曼底。

sentences.en: And this is when a final French embassy appears in England in June 1415.
sentences.zh: 正是在这时，最后一批法国使团于1415年6月出现在英格兰。

sentences.en: Clearly, you know, reports are coming in of what's happening and they're very, very nervous.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道的，有关情况的报告不断传到他们那里，他们感到非常非常紧张。

sentences.en: So they offer Henry pretty generous terms and they are stunned when Henry turns them down.
sentences.zh: 于是他们向亨利提出了相当丰厚的条件，当亨利拒绝时，他们惊呆了。

sentences.en: And the ambassadors leave with two parting shots.
sentences.zh: 大使们带着两句离别时的狠话离开了。

sentences.en: So one of them says to Henry, yeah, you've got all this stuff, but you're not going to do anything with it.
sentences.zh: 其中一人对亨利说，是的，你拥有这一切，但你什么也做不成。

sentences.en: It's going to be a hit and run raid.
sentences.zh: 这只是一次打了就跑的突袭。

sentences.en: You know, you might loot a few fields.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你或许能掠夺几片田地。

sentences.en: You might even capture a town, but you're not going to be able to do anything more than that.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能攻占一座城镇，但除此之外你什么也做不了。

sentences.en: And that is hitting the spot because, of course, that is Henry's worry.
sentences.zh: 这话真戳中要害，因为这当然也是亨利所担忧的。

sentences.en: He doesn't want that to happen.
sentences.zh: 他不希望这种情况发生。

sentences.en: That's your argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的论点。

sentences.en: That was your argument about why he was overrated.
sentences.zh: 这就是你关于他被高估的论点。

sentences.en: That basically it was a fool's errand because France is too big to digeSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上这是一场吃力不讨好的差事，因为法国太大，根本吃不下。

sentences.en: And that no English king can ever hope to do anything other than, you know, sack a town, burn some houses, capture a few knights and then go home again.
sentences.zh: 任何英国国王除了洗劫一座城镇、烧毁几座房屋、俘虏几位骑士然后回家之外，别无他望。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think the French ambassador means less than that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为法国大使的意思不止于此。

sentences.en: I mean, he literally means you will just go and loot a few fields and maybe capture one town.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他字面上的意思是你们只会去掠夺几片田地，也许能占领一个城镇。

sentences.en: And that's what Henry is worried about because that will not rank as a success in the eyes of England and the world.
sentences.zh: 而这正是亨利所担忧的，因为在英格兰乃至全世界看来，这根本算不上成功。

sentences.en: If that is all he can do, he needs to do more than that with all the money, all the men, all the kit that he's prepared.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是他能做到的全部，那么带着他准备的所有资金、所有士兵、所有装备，他必须做得比这更好。

sentences.en: It has to be something more than that.
sentences.zh: 必须有些更大的成效。

sentences.en: And the other parting shot is from a bishop who's travelled with the embassy.
sentences.zh: 另一句狠话来自随使团同行的的一位主教。

sentences.en: And Henry says to the bishop, look, I'm the king of France.
sentences.zh: 亨利对主教说，听着，我是法国国王。

sentences.en: I have a legal right to the crown of France.
sentences.zh: 我对法国王位拥有合法的权利。

sentences.en: And the bishop retorts, our sovereign lord is the true king of France and you have no right to any of the things you claim.
sentences.zh: 主教反唇相讥道，我们的主权君主才是真正的法国国王，你对你声称的一切都没有任何权利。

sentences.en: You are no king, even in England, but merely one claimant among many, jostling for position with the true heirs of the late King Richard.
sentences.zh: 你甚至在英格兰也不是什么国王，不过是众多争权夺利者中的一个，正与已故国王理查的真正继承人争夺地位。

sentences.en: Oh my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I mean, that's punchy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这话真够尖锐的。

sentences.en: Very, very punchy.
sentences.zh: 非常非常尖锐。

sentences.en: That's below the belt, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这简直是戳人痛处，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it may well be because of that, that the revelation that hits Henry a few days later comes as an even greater blow than it already is.
sentences.zh: 也正因如此，几天后降临在亨利身上的那个秘密，可能比表面上看起来对他的打击还要沉重。

sentences.en: And this is the discovery of treason in his own retinue.
sentences.zh: 这就是在他的亲信队伍中发现了叛国阴谋。

sentences.en: Because he's just preparing to embark at Southampton when he is approached by Edmund Mortimer,
sentences.zh: 因为他正准备在南安普顿登船时，埃德蒙·莫蒂弗接近了他，

sentences.en: the Earl of March, who is the guy who people who are opposed to the House of Lancaster think should be king in Henry's place.
sentences.zh: 也就是马奇伯爵，那些反对兰开斯特王朝的人认为他才应该是取代亨利的国王。

sentences.en: Yeah, the alternative claimant.
sentences.zh: 是的，那个备选的王位竞争者。

sentences.en: And Edmund Mortimer comes and he says, look, there's this conspiracy against you and it includes the younger brother of Edward the Duke of York, your own cousin, Richard of York.
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙·莫蒂弗过来对他说，听着，有人在密谋反对你，其中还包括约克公爵爱德华的弟弟、你自己的堂弟理查·约克。

sentences.en: And he is preparing this plot.
sentences.zh: 他正在策划这个阴谋。

sentences.en: He wants to take me, make me king.
sentences.zh: 他想抓住我，让我当国王。

sentences.en: He wants to kill you, get rid of you.
sentences.zh: 他想杀掉你，除掉你。

sentences.en: So, you know, beware.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，小心点。

sentences.en: This is in the footing.
sentences.zh: 这已经在酝酿中了。

sentences.en: And Henry does some investigations and he discovers that, you know, this plot hasn't gone very far.
sentences.zh: 亨利进行了一些调查，发现这个阴谋并没有进展太远。

sentences.en: So it's not looking actually that serious.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上看起来并不是那么严重。

sentences.en: But Richard of York, the guy who's leading this conspiracy, had sounded out one of Henry's closest advisors and friends.
sentences.zh: 但领导这场阴谋的理查·约克，曾试探过亨利最亲密的顾问和朋友之一。

sentences.en: Henry Scroope, who's the nephew of the Archbishop who Henry IV had executed, but had always been kind of very close to Henry V.
sentences.zh: 亨利·斯库普，他是亨利四世处死的那位大主教的侄子，但一直与亨利五世关系非常亲密。

sentences.en: And Scroope had been completely contemptuous of the plot, said it's hopeless, you know, give it up.
sentences.zh: 而斯库普对这个阴谋表现得极其不屑，说这是没用的，你知道的，放弃吧。

sentences.en: But he hadn't revealed it to Henry V.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有向亨利五世透露这件事。

sentences.en: And so Henry is devastated by this.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利对此感到痛心疾首。

sentences.en: And when it's all revealed, he orders the execution, not just of Richard of York, but of Scroope as well.
sentences.zh: 当这一切水落石出时，他下令处决的不仅是理查·约克，还有斯库普。

sentences.en: So this is not a good note on which to be leaving for France.
sentences.zh: 所以这可不是一个启程前往法国的好兆头。

sentences.en: Big old risk by Edmund Mortimer to divulge the details of a plot of which he is the focal point.
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙·莫蒂弗选择泄露一个以他自己为核心的阴谋细节，这真是一场豪赌。

sentences.en: Because Henry could easily have said, well, I'll rub you out as well.
sentences.zh: 因为亨利完全可以说，我也顺便把你给做掉。

sentences.en: You're a threat to me.
sentences.zh: 你对我是个威胁。

sentences.en: Yes, except that, I mean, Edmund Mortimer is doing what Scroope had failed to do.
sentences.zh: 是的，不过话说回来，埃德蒙·莫蒂弗做了斯库普没有做的事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Scroope is executed for not revealing the plot, whereas Mortimer does reveal the plot.
sentences.zh: 斯库普因为没有揭发阴谋而被处决，而莫蒂弗则揭发了阴谋。

sentences.en: And Henry doesn't hold it against him, isn't worried about him.
sentences.zh: 亨利并没有把这记在记恨他，也没有为他担心。

sentences.en: No, and Mortimer is impeccably loyal to Henry V throughout his reign.
sentences.zh: 没有，而且莫蒂弗在亨利五世统治期间一直对他忠心耿耿。

sentences.en: Good for Mortimer.
sentences.zh: 莫蒂弗好样的。

sentences.en: And I guess that this could have winded Henry.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能让亨利备受打击。

sentences.en: And it certainly focuses for him the nature of the risk that he is taking in going to France.
sentences.zh: 这无疑也让他清楚地认识到自己前往法国所承担的风险的本质。

sentences.en: There remain people who see him as a legitimate king.
sentences.zh: 仍然有人视他为合法国王。

sentences.en: There are people who still want to bring the Lancastrian regime down.
sentences.zh: 仍然有人想要推翻兰开斯特政权。

sentences.en: And any hint of failure in France will be potentially fatal for Henry.
sentences.zh: 任何在法国失败的迹象对亨利来说都可能是致命的。

sentences.en: So he knows the gamble that he is taking.
sentences.zh: 所以他很清楚自己在冒什么险。

sentences.en: High risk though, Tom.
sentences.zh: 风险极高啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: Very, very high risk.
sentences.zh: 非常非常高的风险。

sentences.en: But he's off 11th of August, 1415.
sentences.zh: 但他还是出发了，1415年8月11日。

sentences.en: Henry boards the largest ship in England.
sentences.zh: 亨利登上了英格兰最大的船只。

sentences.en: It had just been built for him in Greenwich, the Trinity Royal.
sentences.zh: 这艘船刚刚在格林尼治为他建造好，名为“三位一体皇家号”。

sentences.en: He sails off at the head of a fleet of some 1,500 ships, which as Juliet Barker in her wonderful book on Agincourt points out, was a fleet 12 times the size of the Spanish Armada.
sentences.zh: 他率领着一支由大约1,500艘船组成的舰队起航，正如朱丽叶·巴克在她那本关于阿金库尔的出色著作中所指出的那样，这支舰队的规模是西班牙无敌舰队的12倍。

sentences.en: And as they sail, very few people on the fleet know where they're heading.
sentences.zh: 当他们航行时，舰队中极少数人知道他们要驶向何方。

sentences.en: The French certainly don't know where they're heading.
sentences.zh: 法国人当然也不知道他们要去哪里。

sentences.en: They cross the channel.
sentences.zh: 他们横渡了海峡。

sentences.en: Two days later, the English fleet arrives in the Great Bay at the mouth of the Seine.
sentences.zh: 两天后，英国舰队抵达了塞纳河口的大海湾。

sentences.en: And the ship's moor off a beach off a kind of one of the headlands.
sentences.zh: 船只停泊在某个海岬附近的一处海滩旁。

sentences.en: And it's described by a priest who accompanies Henry on this expedition and who is an absolutely brilliant source for the entire campaign.
sentences.zh: 陪同亨利进行这次远征的一位牧师对这个地方进行了描述，他是整场战役极其出色的历史资料来源。

sentences.en: He describes it as being very stony with large boulders dangerous to ships.
sentences.zh: 他将其描述为布满对船只有危险的大圆石的石滩。

sentences.en: So not the kind of place where a fleet would conventionally moor, but it's been chosen precisely because the French would not expect a landing there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里并不是舰队通常会停泊的地方，但它之所以被选中，恰恰是因为法国人不会料到那里会有人登陆。

sentences.en: And so therefore, there are no defenders.
sentences.zh: 因此，那里也没有防守力量。

sentences.en: And Henry looks out from his flagship at the Seine.
sentences.zh: 亨利从他的旗舰上眺望塞纳河。

sentences.en: There is this rocky beach.
sentences.zh: 那里有一片岩石海滩。

sentences.en: There's a cliff, which is quite easy to climb.
sentences.zh: 有一处悬崖，攀爬起来相当容易。

sentences.en: And it rises about 300 feet to a plateau.
sentences.zh: 它高约300英尺，直通一片高原。

sentences.en: And Henry knows that about three miles beyond that plateau is his target, the port of Harfleur.
sentences.zh: 亨利知道，在那片高原约三英里外就是他的目标——哈弗勒尔港。

sentences.en: What a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 真是个悬念迭起的好地方。

sentences.en: So if you would like to hear the next episode, you're a member of the Rest is History Club, you don't need to do anything because it's right there waiting for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想收听下一集，作为“历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员，你什么都不用做，因为它就在那里等着你。

sentences.en: If you'd like to join the Rest is History Club to hear it right away, the Battle of Harfleur,
sentences.zh: 如果你想加入俱乐部立刻收听关于哈弗勒尔战役的内容，

sentences.en: once more into the breach and all that business, you can sign up at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 再次冲入缺口云云，你可以在therestishistory.com注册。

sentences.en: Otherwise, we will see you next time for the next installment of this thrilling story.
sentences.zh: 否则，我们下期节目再见，继续讲述这个惊心动魄的故事。

sentences.en: Merci, Tom, et au revoir.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆，再见。

sentences.en: À bientôt.
sentences.zh: 回头见。
